admin_audit_http_client.description:
Extends admin_audit with logging of all outgoing HTTP requests made by Nextcloud's internal Guzzle-based HTTP client. Logs include method, URI, status code, HTTP version, request and response headers, cURL transfer statistics, and compression metrics. No UI, no routes — pure audit logging into per-host JSON and plain-text files below a configurable log directory.

aiquila.description:
**AIquila** brings AI into your [Nextcloud](https://nextcloud.com) — private, self-hosted, and under your control. You choose which AI provider processes your data, including models running entirely on your own hardware.

### Nextcloud App

- **Chat** — Converse with an AI assistant about your files and documents
- **Projects** — Scope a conversation to selected folders, so the assistant only sees what you choose
- **Coworkers** — Save repeatable AI jobs and run them on demand or on a schedule
- **Summarise & rewrite** — Condense, draft, rephrase and proofread text
- **Model picker** — Switch provider and model per conversation
- **Usage metrics** — Token and conversation counters exported via OpenMetrics

### Choose your AI provider

Admins enable the providers they want, and can restrict them per user or group:

- **Claude (Anthropic)** — The default, and the most deeply integrated: vision, thinking budgets, native MCP connector, and PDF handling with citations.
- **Hetzner Inference** — OpenAI-compatible API from the German provider Hetzner. Currently an experimental service, free while experimental; Hetzner states it does not store request and response content.
- **Mistral** — French provider, also supporting the native MCP connector. EU-only processing is available through Mistral's regional inference endpoints.
- **Local model** — Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp on your own hardware. Nothing leaves your infrastructure.
- **DeepSeek** — OpenAI-compatible API.

API keys are stored encrypted, and base URLs are admin-only settings. Provider choice
applies to chat and to the Nextcloud Assistant integrations alike. Assistant actions
that send images need a vision-capable provider.

### MCP Server

AIquila includes a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server with 311 tools that gives any MCP client — Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Claude.ai and the Claude mobile app, Cursor, VS Code and others — direct access to your Nextcloud:

- **Files** — Browse, read, write, search, and share
- **Calendar & Tasks** — View, create, and manage events and to-dos
- **Contacts & Mail** — Read and manage address books, accounts, and messages
- **Notes & Recipes** — Create and edit Markdown notes and recipes
- **Bookmarks & Maps** — Manage bookmarks, GPS tracks, favourites, and photos

### Resources

- [Documentation](https://github.com/elgorro/aiquila/blob/main/docs/README.md)
- [Source Code](https://github.com/elgorro/aiquila)
- [Report Issues](https://github.com/elgorro/aiquila/issues)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/elgorro/aiquila/discussions)

---

Built on the [Nextcloud](https://nextcloud.com) open-source community, the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), and the open and commercial AI providers listed above.

# Clock in. Stay within the rules you set.

ArbeitszeitCheck records clock-in, clock-out and breaks on the Nextcloud you already host. Pick a country profile for Germany (ArbZG), Austria (AZG/ARG) or Switzerland (ArG), match holiday regions, approve absences, run reports (including DATEV) and keep an audit log.

Also listed as **TimeGuard** in some App Store searches.

**Free web app** (AGPL-3.0-or-later). Companion apps: https://nextcloud.software-by-design.de/

## Why teams install it

- **Start and stop work cleanly** — pauses, resume, manual entries with a reason
- **Match your country** — DE / AT / CH profiles with Länder, Bundesländer or cantons
- **See break and rest issues early** — technical checks against the profile you configured
- **Run absences properly** — vacation, illness, special and unpaid leave with approval; entitlement modes and CSV import via `occ`
- **Report what happened** — employee, team and manager views; overtime and absence reports; DATEV export
- **Lock a month when you need to** — optional finalization with snapshot, hash and PDF; admin reopen with a reason
- **Control access** — open to all users or allow-lists; Nextcloud admins keep access

## Clear limits

- This app is **not legal advice**. You stay responsible for working-time models, collective agreements, configuration and how recorded data is used. Ask counsel when needed.
- Technical violation reports against your profile are not a third-party certification.
- Declared databases: MySQL and PostgreSQL. Nextcloud 32–35, PHP 8.1–8.5.

## Feedback welcome

We improve this app with real-world use. Bug reports, rough edges, and ideas help — open a GitHub Issue (https://github.com/aSoftwareByDesignRepository/nextcloud-arbeitszeitcheck/issues) or write to info@software-by-design.de. Your feedback directly shapes what we build next.

assistant.description:
This app brings a user interface to use the Nextcloud text processing feature.

It allows users to launch AI tasks, be notified when they finish and see the results.
The assistant also appears in others apps like Text to easily process parts of a document.

More details on the assistant OCS API and frontend integration possibilities in the
[developer doc](https://github.com/nextcloud/assistant/raw/main/docs/developer)

### How to use it

A new right header menu entry appears. Once clicked, the assistant is displayed and you can select and task type and
set the input you want to process.

The task might run immediately or be scheduled depending on the time estimation given by the AI provider.
Once a task is scheduled, it will run as a background job. When it is finished, you will receive a notification
from which the results can be displayed.

Other apps can integrate with the assistant. For example, Text will display an inline button besides every paragraph
to directly select a task type to process this paragraph. Selecting a task this way will open the assistant with the task
being pre-selected and the input text set.

More details and screenshots in the [user doc](https://github.com/nextcloud/assistant/raw/main/docs/user).

## Features

In the assistant, the list of available tasks depends on the available providers installed via other apps.
This means you have complete freedom over which service/software will actually run your AI tasks.

### Text processing providers

So far, the [Local Large language model](https://github.com/nextcloud/llm2#readme)
and the [OpenAi/LocalAI integration](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/integration_openai) apps
include text processing providers to:
* Summarize
* Extract topics
* Generate a headline
* Get an answer from a free prompt
* Reformulate (OpenAi/LocalAi only)
* Context writer: Generate text with a specified style. The style can be described or provided via an example text.

### Text to image (Image generation)

Known providers:
* [OpenAi/LocalAI integration](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/integration_openai)
* [Text2Image Stable Diffusion](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/text2image_stablediffusion)

### Speech to text (Audio transcription)

Known providers:
* [OpenAi/LocalAI integration](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/integration_openai)
* [Local Whisper Speech-To-Text](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/stt_whisper)

astrolabe.description:
# Astrolabe - Semantic Search for Nextcloud

Find your content by meaning, not just keywords. Astrolabe brings AI-powered semantic search to your Nextcloud, helping you discover documents, notes, calendar events, and files through natural language.

## Features

- **Semantic Search**: Search across Notes, Files, Calendar, Deck, and more using natural language queries
- **Unified Search Integration**: Results appear in Nextcloud's global search bar alongside traditional results
- **Background Indexing**: Your content is automatically indexed for instant semantic search
- **Vector Visualization**: Explore your content in an interactive 2D visualization showing semantic relationships
- **Hybrid Search**: Combines semantic understanding with keyword matching for best results

## How It Works

Astrolabe connects to a semantic search service that understands the meaning of your content. Instead of exact keyword matches, you can search for concepts - ask "meeting notes from last week" or "recipes with chicken" and find relevant documents even if they don't contain those exact words.

## Getting Started

1. Install and enable the app
2. Grant background access to allow indexing of your content
3. Start searching with natural language in Nextcloud's search bar

See [documentation](https://github.com/cbcoutinho/astrolabe) for configuration details.

# AudioCheck — your audio library inside Nextcloud

Your audio files already live in Files. AudioCheck indexes the folders you choose and streams them with live permission checks.

The app is **free** under AGPL-3.0-or-later. There is no seat license for this web app in the shipped package.

## What you get

- Separate music and audiobook library roots; collections, albums and folder browsing
- Multi-file audiobooks as one queue; resume stored on your server per account
- Durable playback queue; optional resume on open; Continue listening on Home and the dashboard widget
- Playlists; Favorites synced with Files stars
- Chapter jumps on M4B (and tagged chapter metadata); playback speed 0.5×–4.0×
- Files actions: Play in AudioCheck / Play folder as album
- Browse by artists, authors, genres, series, folders, tags and favorites
- Optional access restriction (Nextcloud admins always retain access)
- UI languages: German (Sie-Form), English, French, Spanish, Danish, Dutch, Italian, Polish, Swedish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Brazilian Portuguese (every shipped UI string lives in `l10n`)
- Accessibility foundations aimed at WCAG 2.1 AA (not a third-party certification)

## Formats

**Indexed and streamed on the server:** MP3, MP4/M4A/M4B (including podcasts tagged as video/mp4), OGG, Opus, FLAC, WAV, AAC and other common `audio/*` types.

**Browser playback** depends on the browser: MP3, M4A, M4B, AAC, OGG, Opus and WAV usually work; FLAC and some others may need a different browser.

## Get started

1. Open **Library**, add music and audiobook folders, then **Scan now** (or `occ audiocheck:scan`).
2. In **Settings**, enable **Resume where you left off** if you want that behaviour.
3. Open **Music** or **Audiobooks** and press Play.

## Honest limits

- Playback bytes go through a single file-access gate with live permission checks; revoked shares stop playback. The app makes no outbound HTTP calls for playback.
- After a full browser navigation away from AudioCheck, browsers may require a click to resume audio.
- Scan depth is capped (32 folder levels). Playlist play/shuffle has a documented track cap (2000).
- Declared databases: MySQL and PostgreSQL only.

## Feedback welcome

We improve this app with real-world use. Bug reports, rough edges, and ideas help — open a GitHub Issue (https://github.com/aSoftwareByDesignRepository/nextcloud-audiocheck/issues) or write to info@software-by-design.de. Your feedback directly shapes what we build next.

## Requirements

- Nextcloud 32–35
- PHP 8.2–8.5
- MySQL or PostgreSQL

auto_groups.description:
Automatically add users to the specified Auto Groups, except those users belonging to one of the specified Override Groups. 
Optionally, the group assignment can be triggered on every successful login, which is useful for external user backends.

## Configuration

- Go to "Settings > Administration > Additional settings"
- Configure the Auto Groups
- If required, configure the Override Groups (e.g., for Service Accounts)
- Optionally, enable the Login Hook, which will enforce correct group membership on every successful login

Note that this app prevents group deletions for groups referenced as Auto Groups or Override Groups.

## Comparison to similar Apps

* [Everyone Group](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/group_everyone): The "Everyone Group" app adds a virtual Group Backend, always returning all users. In contrast, "Auto Groups" operates on "real" groups in your normal Group Backend. Additionally, it is possible to specify Override Groups which will prevent users from being added to the Auto Group(s).
* [Default Group](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/defaultgroup): "Auto Groups" is actually a modernized and maintaned fork of "Default Group", which seems to be abandoned since NC12 or so. In terms of functionality, they are almost identical.

budgetcheck.description:
# BudgetCheck

Scoped finance for Nextcloud. Each **workspace** is either a **household** (recurring monthly rhythm with budgets, savings targets, and yearly overview) or a **bounded project** (project window, period overview, optional cap warning).

Every workspace has its own ledger, categories, members, and tax settings. The **server is the source of truth** for all calculations; amounts are stored in **minor units**, never as floating-point. **Monthly close** produces an immutable snapshot with a verifiable calculation hash; controlled reopen restores editing. Optional **tax-aware** mode supports net or gross entry with deterministic VAT conversion.

The UI is **workspace-scoped** (household and project totals never mix), targets **WCAG 2.1 AA**, full keyboard use, and responsive layouts from **320px** width.

## Feedback welcome

We improve this app with real-world use. Bug reports, rough edges, and ideas help — open a GitHub Issue (https://github.com/aSoftwareByDesignRepository/nextcloud-budgetcheck/issues) or write to info@software-by-design.de. Your feedback directly shapes what we build next.

Nextcloud Cospend is a group/shared budget manager. It was inspired by the great [IHateMoney](https://github.com/spiral-project/ihatemoney/).

You can use it when you share a house, when you go on vacation with friends, whenever you share expenses with a group of people.

It lets you create projects with members and bills. Each member has a balance computed from the project bills. Balances are not an absolute amount of money at members disposal but rather a relative information showing if a member has spent more for the group than the group has spent for her/him, independently of exactly who spent money for whom. This way you can see who owes the group and who the group owes. Ultimately you can ask for a settlement plan telling you which payments to make to reset members balances.

Project members are independent from Nextcloud users. Projects can be shared with other Nextcloud users or via public links.

[MoneyBuster](https://gitlab.com/eneiluj/moneybuster) Android client is [available in F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/net.eneiluj.moneybuster/) and on the [Play store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.eneiluj.moneybuster).

cromcull.description:
CromCull finds byte-identical duplicate files across your Nextcloud storage and lets you decide what to do about them.

**How it works:**
- Size-bucket pre-filter using Nextcloud's existing file cache (no re-scanning)
- Partial hash (first 64KB, SHA-256) to cheaply eliminate non-matches
- Full-file SHA-256 to confirm exact duplicates
- Persistent hash cache uses Nextcloud's edit tracking to skip re-hashing unchanged files — repeat scans are significantly faster, especially on external storage
- The first scan reads and hashes every file (a good overnight task for large libraries); after that, the cache keeps things fast

**Safety first:**
- CromCull never deletes anything automatically
- Every deletion is an explicit, per-file human decision
- All deletions go through Nextcloud's own trash bin, protected by live re-verification before every delete
- Group folders and shared files are blocked from deletion
- A permanent CSV audit log records every action

**Features:**
- Chunked scanning with progress bar and cancel support
- Per-group Recheck button to re-verify a single group without a full rescan
- Hide/Un-Hide duplicate groups per-user, keyed on content hash so future copies are automatically hidden
- Configurable size filters and extension ignore lists
- Folder exclusions via marker files that travel with renamed/moved folders
- Review UI with per-file external links for side-by-side comparison
- Batch delete across multiple groups with confirmation modal
- Admin hash cache management panel with entry count and full cache clear
- `cromcull:status` occ command for CLI visibility into scan state and cache stats

In proprietary environments, changes in events and contacts are nowadays usually pushed to other clients so that they can update their views almost in real-time.

WebDAV however (and in this context, especially CalDAV and CardDAV) doesn't currently support push notifications of clients when a collection has changed. So clients have to periodically ask the server for changes. This causes unnecessary delays and battery usage.

The WebDAV-Push standard, which is currently in development, wants to solve this problem with an open protocol, too.

This is the server part of these efforts to draft a standard and provide a working implementation (server + client) in order to demonstrate it.


The current WebDAV-Push draft is provided by [@bitfireAT](https://github.com/bitfireAT).

diskmap.description:
DiskMap shows where storage is going across your Nextcloud instance — per user and per team
folder — without scanning anything.

Nextcloud already tracks aggregated folder sizes in its file cache, updated on every operation.
DiskMap is a visualizer over data that already exists: it never triggers a filesystem scan.

Each view pairs a WinDirStat-style treemap with an expandable folder tree, kept in sync both
ways: click a tile on the map and the tree opens to that file, click a row in the tree and the
map highlights its region.

**For administrators:**
- Whole-server view: every account, team folder and external storage as a top-level entry,
  browsable down to individual files.
- Team folders overview: used space, quota and occupancy, with a files / trash / versions
  breakdown for each folder.

**For every user:**
- The same treemap and folder tree over your own storage, with quota occupancy and a
  files / trash / versions breakdown.

All figures show the timestamp of the underlying file cache entry, so it's always clear this
reflects what Nextcloud's cache knows, not a live disk read.

end_to_end_encryption.description:
## **End-to-End Encryption**

### For End Users

**Protect your most sensitive files with strong encryption.**

The End-to-End Encryption app gives you complete control over your data privacy.
With this app, you can encrypt specific folders so that only you (and those you trust) can access their contents.
Your files are encrypted on your device before they reach the server, ensuring that no one—not even the server administrator—can read them.

**Benefits:**
- 🔒 **True privacy**: Files are encrypted on your device and can only be decrypted by you
- 📱 **Works across all platforms**: Fully supported on desktop, Android, iOS clients, and as you wish even in the browser
- 🎯 **Selective encryption**: Choose which folders to encrypt
- 🛡️ **Secure sharing**: Share encrypted files with other users or even secure public upload using the encrypted file drop

---

### For Administrators

**Enterprise-ready end-to-end encryption infrastructure for your Nextcloud instance.**

This app provides all the necessary server-side APIs and infrastructure to enable End-to-End encryption (E2EE) for your users.
It ensures that encrypted data remains secure throughout its lifecycle on your server.

**Technical highlights:**
- 🔐 **Complete API suite**: Provides all client-side APIs needed for E2EE implementation
- 🔒 **Secure FileDrop integration**: Enables secure file sharing with encryption
- 🛡️ **Zero-knowledge architecture**: Server never has access to encryption keys
- ⚙️ **Group restrictions**: Limit app usage to specific user groups if needed
- 🔄 **Background job management**: Automatic rollback handling for failed operations

### Setup
This application provides the server-side infrastructure for end-to-end encryption, but it requires client support to function.
To enable end-to-end encryption, users will need to install the corresponding client-side app on their devices (desktop, Android, iOS) or use the web client.

Using the web interface, after enabling it in the personal settings, allows you to encrypt files and folders directly in the browser,
providing a seamless experience without needing additional software. But also requires some kind of trust in the server as the code is delivered by the server and could be manipulated.

Once enable through clients or the web interface, you can create encrypted folders and upload or move files into them.
The clients and the web interface will handle the encryption and decryption processes automatically.

⚠️ This comes with some limitations and caveats, as only normal file operations can be handled.
Meaning that some apps in the web interface do not work with encrypted files.

# EPUB Viewer
EPUB Viewer is an ebook reader based on pure javascript renderers. It works for publications formatted according to the following standards:

 - [EPUB]
 - [PDF]
 - [CBR and CBZ] ('comics')

EPUB files are displayed using the futurepress [epub.js] renderer to provide near-native looks, especially when used full-screen. Turn pages by pressing the left/right hand side of the screen/window or using the cursor keys (if you have those), use the sidebar to browse through chapters or bookmarks and add annotations.

PDF is handled by Mozilla's [pdf.js] renderer in combination with a custom reader app to enable side-by-side display, batch search and more. Controls are like those used in the Epub renderer with a few exceptions, e.g. night mode has not been implemented yet.

CBR and CBZ are supported using a custom renderer inspired by [balaclark]'s work. As with Epub, books can be navigated using the keyboard as well as mouse or touch navigation. Reader generates a visual index of all pages, show in the sidebar (thumbnail generation can be disabled for low-memory and/or -speed devices). As CBx files are often of varying quality, a set of image enhancement filters are provided.

Comic pages may use JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP. TIFF pages are not supported.

See [README] for more exhaustive information on features and potential misfeatures of this app.

   [epub.js]: https://github.com/futurepress/epub.js
   [EPUB]: http://idpf.org/epub
   [CBR and CBZ]: https://wiki.mobileread.com/wiki/CBR_and_CBZ
   [balaclark]: https://github.com/balaclark/HTML5-Comic-Book-Reader

eva_ai.description:
Eva AI turns your Nextcloud into a private, searchable knowledge base powered by Large Language Models. Ask questions in natural language and get instant, cited answers drawn from your own files — fully local with Ollama, or optionally via Groq for cloud-hosted inference.

## Why Eva AI?

Your data stays yours. No third-party indexing, no external databases, no cloud required. Eva runs entirely within your Nextcloud instance, giving you full control over your files and conversations.

## Key Features

**Intelligent File Indexing**
Eva automatically reads, chunks, and embeds your files for semantic search. Supports a wide range of formats: plain text (txt, md, csv, json, xml, yaml, sql, ...), PDF, Microsoft Office (docx/xlsx/pptx with macros and templates), OpenDocument (odt/ods/odp), EPUB, saved mail (eml, mbox), web archives (mht/mhtml), Jupyter notebooks (ipynb), and many more. A file that cannot be read is skipped instead of stopping the run.

**Hybrid Retrieval Engine**
Combines vector-based semantic search with lexical search (BM25) using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) to deliver the most relevant results — even for exact-match queries.

**Cited Sources**
Every answer includes the exact file path where the information was found, so you can always verify the source. Answers that used the web list the pages they actually retrieved, with their site and an excerpt, marked as web sources.

**Nextcloud Integration**
Eva can perform actions directly within Nextcloud: search for files, create documents, rename items, and work with templates across your entire home space — including Notes and Contacts.

**Ollama and Groq Support**
Start fully local with Ollama (no configuration required) or optionally connect to Groq for cloud-hosted inference. Embeddings always run locally via Ollama.

**Zero Configuration**
Just install and go. Eva automatically detects your local Ollama instance and selects appropriate models.

**Talk Integration**
Optionally integrate with Nextcloud Talk for conversational AI within your chat rooms.

## Requirements

- Nextcloud 30–35
- PHP 8.2+
- [Ollama](https://ollama.com) running locally (default: http://localhost:11434)
- Optional: Groq API key for cloud-hosted inference

## Get Started

1. Install the app
2. Ensure Ollama is running on your server
3. Open Eva from the left sidebar
4. Start chatting with your files

## Privacy

With Ollama, all processing happens on your server. Your files never leave your infrastructure. No analytics, no telemetry, no external calls.

- Issues: https://github.com/SchBenedikt/nextcloud-ai/issues

files_accesscontrol.description:
Nextcloud's File Access Control app enables administrators to protect data from unauthorized access or modifications.

## How it works
The administrator can create and manage a set of rule groups. Each of the rule groups consists of one or more rules. If all rules of a group hold true, the group matches the request and access is being denied or the upload is blocked. The rules criteria range from IP address, MIME type and request time to group membership, tags, user agent and more.

An example would be to deny access to MS Excel/XLSX files owned by the "Human Resources" group accessed from an IP not on the internal company network or to block uploads of files bigger than 512 mb by students in the "1st year" group.

Learn more about File Access Control on [https://nextcloud.com/workflow](https://nextcloud.com/workflow)

files_antivirus.description:
Antivirus for files is an antivirus app for Nextcloud.

* 🕵️‍♂️ When the user uploads a file, it's checked
* ☢️ Uploaded and infected files will be deleted and a notification will be shown and/or sent via email
* 🔎 Background Job to scan all files
* ❓ Use ClamAV (open source), Kaspersky Scan Engine or an ICAP compatible scanner

This application inspects files that are uploaded to Nextcloud for viruses before they are written to the Nextcloud storage. If a file is identified as a virus, it is either logged or not uploaded to the server. The application relies on the underlying ClamAV virus scanning engine, which the admin points Nextcloud to when configuring the application. Alternatively, a Kaspersky Scan Engine can be configured, which has to run on a separate server.
For this app to be effective, the ClamAV virus definitions should be kept up to date. Also note that enabling this app will impact system performance as additional processing is required for every upload. More information is available in the Antivirus documentation.

files_automatedtagging.description:
An app for Nextcloud that automatically assigns tags to newly uploaded files based on some conditions.

The tags can later be used to control retention, file access, automatic script execution and more.

## How it works
To define tags, administrators can create and manage a set of rule groups. Each rule group consists of one or more rules combined through operators. Rules can include criteria like file type, size, time and more. A request matches a group if all rules evaluate to true. On uploading a file all defined groups are evaluated and when matching, the given tags are assigned to the file.

files_autorename.description:
AutoRename is a Nextcloud app that renames and organizes newly added or moved files based on user-defined rules.
By placing a `.rename.conf` file in a folder, users can specify regex-based patterns to rename or move files.

Renaming is handled by a background job that runs every few minutes, so changes may not be immediate.

Features:
- 📝 Define renaming rules using powerful regular expressions.
- 📂 Move files to subfolders specified in the new name (e.g., `subfolder/new_name`).
- 📅 Insert metadata like dates, EXIF data, or file modification times into filenames using [placeholders](https://github.com/powerflo/files_autorename/tree/main?tab=readme-ov-file#what-placeholders-can-i-use-in-the-replacement-string).
- 🔍 Extract [text from PDFs](https://github.com/powerflo/files_autorename/tree/main?tab=readme-ov-file#pdfPatternMatch) for custom filenames.
- 🔄 Transform filenames to [uppercase or lowercase](https://github.com/powerflo/files_autorename/tree/main?tab=readme-ov-file#how-do-i-rename-files-with-upperlowercase-changes).

Quick Start

1. Place a `.rename.conf` file in the desired folder.
2. Add a rule like this:
    ```
    ^Invoice_(\d{4})_(\d{2})\.pdf$:Invoices/$1/$2/$0
    ```
3. Upload a matching file (e.g., `Invoice_2025_04.pdf`) — it will be renamed to `Invoices/2025/04/Invoice_2025_04.pdf` during the next background job run.

Check out the [full documentation on GitHub](https://github.com/powerflo/files_autorename).

files_sharing_raw.description:
Raw Fileserver (**`files_sharing_raw`**) serves files **as-is** so you can link directly to the file itself (i.e. without any of Nextcloud's UI). This makes it easy to host static web pages, RSS feeds, images, or other assets and embed/link them elsewhere.

## Design goals

* **Minimal**: deliver bytes, not UI.
* **Fast**: keep server work low (good for assets).
* **Quiet failures**: plain 404 Not found (text/plain) for invalid/missing public shares (no Nextcloud HTML error pages), ideal for asset fetches.
* **Privacy-friendly**: **cookie-free responses** (best effort).
* **Allowlist-gated:** public raw access is opt-in — only explicitly enabled public share tokens are served.
* **Secure by default**: strict CSP with optional per-scope overrides. *)
* **Streaming by default**: for normal `GET` (`200`) responses, the body is streamed whenever possible instead of loading the entire file into memory.

*) For security and privacy, the content is served with a configurable [Content-Security-Policy][] (CSP) header, allowing different policies per share token, path, file extension, or MIME type (with a safe hardcoded fallback).

[Content-Security-Policy]: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Security-Policy

## Usage

The common usage is to first share a file and enable public access through a link. In the Advanced settings of this share (in the right sidebar), the Raw link must be enabled. If the share link is `https://my-nextcloud/s/aBc123DeF456xyZ`, then this app will provide access to the raw file at `https://my-nextcloud/raw/aBc123DeF456xyZ`. If the share is a folder, the files within it are accessible as e.g. `https://my-nextcloud/raw/aBc123DeF456xyZ/path/to/file`.

A user can also access their own private files. For example, a file named `test.html` in anansi's Documents folder would be available at `https://my-nextcloud/raw/u/anansi/Documents/test.html`.

fileviewer.description:
# Universal File Viewer

Universal File Viewer is a Nextcloud app that registers [Flyfish File Viewer](https://github.com/flyfish-dev/file-viewer) as a handler for
the 200+ file types supported by Flyfish.

The app renders files in a sandboxed iframe. The parent Nextcloud Viewer component
fetches the selected file with the authenticated Viewer URL and transfers the file
Blob over a document-bound `MessageChannel`. The default sandbox intentionally does
not include `allow-same-origin`. EPUB files use a two-stage bootstrap that commits
the renderer to an opaque `blob:null` document before any file bytes are transferred.
The renderer cannot read the parent Nextcloud document, while EPUB chapter content
stays in a nested iframe that allows its own origin but deliberately does not allow
scripts.

## Supported Formats

Universal File Viewer uses [Flyfish Viewer](https://github.com/flyfish-dev/file-viewer) and thus supports 200+ formats:
[supported formats](https://github.com/flyfish-dev/file-viewer/blob/main/README.en.md#supported-formats)
matrix.

| Category | Extensions |
| --- | --- |
| Word | `docx`, `docm`, `dotx`, `dotm` |
| Legacy Word | `doc`, `dot` |
| Compatible documents | `rtf`, `odt` |
| Excel | `xlsx`, `xltx` |
| Excel-compatible | `xlsm`, `xlsb`, `xls`, `xlt`, `xltm`, `csv`, `tsv`, `ods`, `fods`, `numbers` |
| PowerPoint | `ppt`, `pptx`, `pptm`, `potx`, `potm`, `ppsx`, `ppsm`, `odp` |
| PDF | `pdf` |
| OFD | `ofd` |
| Typst | `typ`, `typst` |
| Archives | `zip`, `zipx`, `7z`, `rar`, `tar`, `gz`, `tgz`, `bz2`, `xz`, `zst`, `cab`, `iso`, `jar`, `apk`, `cbz`, `cbr`, and more |
| Compiled HTML Help | `chm` |
| Binary inspection | `bin`, `hex`, `elf`, `exe`, `dll`, `class`, `macho` |
| Email | `eml`, `msg`, `mbox` |
| EDA | `olb`, `dra`, `gds`, `oas`, `oasis` |
| CAD | `dwg`, `dxf`, `dwf`, `dwfx`, `xps` |
| Geospatial data | `geojson`, `kml`, `gpx`, `shp` |
| 3D models | `glb`, `gltf`, `obj`, `stl`, `ply`, `fbx`, `dae`, `3ds`, `3mf`, `amf`, `usd`, `usda`, `usdc`, `usdz`, `kmz`, `pcd`, `wrl`, `vrml`, `xyz`, `vtk`, `vtp`, `step`, `stp`, `iges`, `igs`, `ifc`, `3dm` |
| XMind mind maps | `xmind` |
| Excalidraw | `excalidraw` |
| draw.io | `drawio`, `dio` |
| Mermaid | `mermaid`, `mmd` |
| PlantUML | `plantuml`, `puml` |
| EPUB | `epub` |
| UMD ebook | `umd` |
| Markdown | `md`, `markdown` |
| Images | `gif`, `jpg`, `jpeg`, `bmp`, `tiff`, `tif`, `png`, `svg`, `webp`, `avif`, `ico`, `heic`, `heif`, `jxl` |
| Source and text | `txt`, `json`, `jsonc`, `json5`, `ipynb`, `js`, `mjs`, `cjs`, `css`, `java`, `py`, `html`, `htm`, `jsx`, `ts`, `tsx`, `xml`, `log`, `vue`, `yaml`, `yml`, `toml`, `ini`, `proto`, `hcl`, `tex`, `gv`, `http`, `sh`, `bash`, `sql`, `go`, `rs`, `rb`, `swift`, `kt`, `react`, `php`, `c`, `cpp`, `cc`, `h`, `hpp`, `cs`, `diff`, `patch`, `bundle`, `bdl` |
| Audio | `mp3`, `mpeg`, `wav`, `ogg`, `oga`, `opus`, `m4a`, `aac`, `flac`, `weba`, `midi`, `mid` |
| Video | `mp4`, `webm`, `m3u8` |
| Adobe and design assets | `psd`, `psb`, `pdd`, `psdt`, `ai`, `ait`, `eps`, `ps`, `idml`, `icml`, `idms`, `inx`, `fla`, `xfl`, `xd`, `indd`, `indt`, `ase`, `aco`, `abr`, `csh`, `pat`, `grd`, `asl` |
| Medical images | `dcm`, `dicom` |
| Signatures and evidence containers | `p7m`, `p7s`, `p7c`, `p7b`, `pkcs7`, `cms`, `cmsc`, `tsd`, `tst`, `tsq`, `tsr`, `asics`, `scs`, `asice`, `sce`, `ers`, `asc`, `sig`, `pgp`, `gpg`, `jws` |
| Fonts and data assets | `ttf`, `otf`, `woff`, `woff2`, `sqlite`, `wasm`, `parquet`, `avro`, `webarchive` |

## File format settings

The administration page exposes human-readable format groups such as JPEG (`.jpg`,
`.jpeg`), Markdown (`.md`, `.markdown`), and EPUB (`.epub`). It does not expose raw
MIME type strings.

Universal File Viewer keeps Flyfish's supported-extension inventory, then resolves
those extensions through Nextcloud's effective extension-to-MIME mapping using
`OCP\Files\IMimeTypeDetector::getAllMappings()`. During installation, upgrades, and
re-enabling, the app adds fallback mappings for supported extensions that are absent
from both Nextcloud core and the administrator's `mimetypemapping.json`.
Administrator entries always win. The app tracks its exact additions, yields when
Nextcloud later gains a core mapping, and removes only unchanged app-owned entries during uninstall. The
resulting deduplicated MIME types are used internally when registering the Viewer
handler.

When several supported extensions resolve to the same MIME type, Nextcloud Viewer
cannot dispatch them independently. The settings page therefore combines them into
one option and lists every affected extension. Shared aliases keep their format name,
such as JPEG, while distinct formats use an explicit label such as `DOC/DOT`. Saved
preferences use stable app-specific format identifiers; existing `disabled_mimes`
preferences are migrated against the current Nextcloud mapping.

## Sandbox

The default sandbox is:

```text
allow-scripts allow-downloads allow-forms allow-modals allow-popups allow-presentation
```

For `.epub` files, an HTTP bootstrap starts with the stricter `allow-scripts`
sandbox and creates the final renderer Blob from a fixed application template. The
parent briefly grants `allow-same-origin` only while that already-opaque bootstrap
navigates to its `blob:null` URL. A small renderer gate establishes a
document-bound `MessageChannel`; the parent then restores the strict sandbox before
loading Flyfish or transferring the EPUB. The gate probes whether the browser can
still create the readable nested chapter iframe EPUB.js requires. Chromium and
Firefox pass this probe. Current WebKit/Safari fails closed with an explanatory
error instead of retaining an outer sandbox configuration that could become
same-origin after a later navigation.

Flyfish and EPUB.js render untrusted chapter content in a nested iframe whose
sandbox contains `allow-same-origin` but not `allow-scripts`, so chapter scripts and
event handlers cannot run. The outer renderer remains opaque and cannot read the
parent Nextcloud document. Once its final load is confirmed over the bound channel,
any later outer-frame navigation disconnects and removes the viewer. The browser
test suite checks the origin boundary, publisher styling, script isolation,
fail-closed behavior, and unexpected-navigation handling; Flyfish and EPUB.js
upgrades should be treated as security-sensitive changes.

Other file types keep the configured outer sandbox unchanged. Switching across the
EPUB boundary closes the old channel, rotates its token, and replaces the iframe so
the browser applies the new origin policy to a fresh document.

Parser workers do not run in the parent Nextcloud page. For PDF, DOCX-family,
PPTX-family, DWG, STEP/IGES/BREP, specialist binary/design/DICOM/signature formats,
and spreadsheet files of at least 1 MiB, the frame fetches the
exact configured bundled worker without credentials, creates a frame-owned `blob:`
URL, and starts the worker from inside the sandbox. Under the default sandbox these
workers have the opaque `null` origin. Libarchive formats use the same frame-owned
`blob:` isolation model. Legacy PPT uses Flyfish's asynchronous direct path because
its integrity-verifying Worker requires Web Crypto, which Chromium does not expose
to an opaque `blob:null` Worker. Smaller spreadsheet files and legacy PPT parse on
the iframe's main thread, which is also sandboxed.

The only default-page CSP additions are `frame-src 'self' blob:`, and they are added
only to responses that dispatch Nextcloud's Viewer-loading event. The app does not
add instance-wide worker, connection, WebAssembly-eval, style, image, font, or media
allowances. The direct iframe response has its own scoped CSP for local assets,
frame-owned `blob:` workers, renderer-required evaluation and WebAssembly, and the
configured geospatial tile origin. The EPUB bootstrap uses a separate, narrower CSP
without geospatial origins.

If a deployment needs to trade isolation for non-EPUB compatibility with specific
browser worker or WASM behavior, administrators can override the general sandbox.
EPUB always uses the hardened bootstrap and does not fall back to a same-origin
Nextcloud document:

```bash
occ config:app:set fileviewer sandbox --value="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-downloads allow-forms allow-modals allow-popups allow-presentation"
```

findling.description:
What Findling does:
- Full text search in the normal Nextcloud search bar
- OCR for scanned PDFs and images: nine languages available, German, English and French are the default
- Semantic search: finds documents through paraphrases
- Every result is permission-checked by Nextcloud
- No configuration: the first index run starts on its own
- Privacy: everything runs locally, no telemetry, nothing leaves your server

Together with the [Nextcloud MCP Connector](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/mcp_connector), Findling forms the retrieval layer for your own RAG: AI assistants search your document contents with exactly the rights of the asking user, and no content leaves your server.

Supported file types:
- PDF (scanned too), DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, ODT, ODS, ODP
- HTML, RTF, TXT, Markdown, CSV
- Images through OCR: JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP

Requirements:
- Nextcloud 33 to 35, apps: AppAPI, Findling Backend (External Apps), Findling
- RAM: 4 GB is enough, 731.9 MB resident after an index run, under a hard 2 GB limit (measured)
- CPU: 2 cores are enough, amd64 and arm64

Enterprise support and paid add-ons: request a quote at admin@infranode.dev

flow_notifications.description:
Enable users to configure notifications with customized conditions in their Flow configuration.

Users are empowered to configure a "Send a notification" Flow in their personal settings. They can choose between the events being triggered, and other conditions like filetypes, assigned tags, time ranges and more. They can specify an inscription so that when the notification appears they will have context.

To use the `Flow Notifications` app, ensure that the `Notifications` app is installed and enabled. The `Notifications` app provides the necessary APIs for the `Flow Notifications` app to work correctly.

![Notification Flow Configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nextcloud/flow_notifications/master/screenshots/configuration.png)

When an event happens where all conditions are apply, the user will receive a regular Nextcloud notification.

![Flow Notification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nextcloud/flow_notifications/master/screenshots/notification.png)

forms.description:
**Simple surveys and questionnaires, self-hosted!**

- **📝 Simple design:** No mass of options, only the essentials. Works well on mobile of course.
- **📊 View & export results:** Results are visualized and can also be exported as CSV in the same format used by Google Forms.
- **🔒 Data under your control!** Unlike in Google Forms, Typeform, Doodle and others, the survey info and responses are kept private on your instance.
- **🧑‍💻 Connect to your software:** Easily integrate Forms into your service with our full-fledged [REST-API](https://github.com/nextcloud/forms/blob/main/docs/API_v3.md).
- **🙋 Get involved!** We have lots of stuff planned like more question types, collaboration on forms, [and much more](https://github.com/nextcloud/forms/milestones)!

formulabase.description:
FormulaBase is a lightweight personal calculator for the formulas you use again and again — markups, unit conversions, loan payments, mixing ratios, engineering constants, anything.

Organise your formulas into collections, define each formula's variables once, then open it any time, type in numbers, and read the result live. The math runs entirely in your browser (no eval, no server round-trip).

Features:
- Nearly 3,000 built-in formula templates across 63 categories (physics, geometry, finance, health, chemistry, electricity, astronomy, computing, and many more) — searchable, and ready to drop into your own collections
- Collections of reusable formulas
- Named variables with labels, units and default values
- Safe expression engine: + - * / % ^, parentheses, and functions (sqrt, round, floor, ceil, abs, min, max, pow, log, ln, sin, cos, tan, pi, e)
- Live result as you type, with unit and decimal-place control
- Version history per formula — the version before each edit is kept beside it, numbered and restorable, separate from the calculation history
- Share a collection with other Nextcloud users at three levels (view / edit / delete)
- Same clean, themable design as RegiBase (light / dark)

The template library is large (3,122 formulas) and not all of it has been hand-verified. If you spot a wrong formula, bad default, mistranslation, or missing unit, please open an issue on GitHub — reports are welcome.

formvox.description:
FormVox is a file-based forms and polls app for Nextcloud. Unlike traditional form apps, FormVox stores everything in .fvform files — no database tables needed.

**Features:**
* 100% file-based storage (.fvform files)
* Question types: text, textarea, single/multiple choice, dropdown, date, time, number, scale, rating, file upload, matrix, table
* Conditional logic and page routing
* Quiz mode with scoring
* Export to CSV, JSON, and ODT (with custom template support)
* Import from Microsoft Forms
* Per-form branding with visual page builder
* Answer piping (use previous answers in later questions)
* Charts and visualizations in Results view
* Webhooks and REST API for integrations
* Collaborative editing with real-time presence indicators
* Notifications on new responses
* Password protection and expiration for public links
* Multi-language: English, Dutch, German, French

**Unique Benefits:**
* One file contains everything (definition + responses)
* Works with Nextcloud's versioning and sharing
* End-to-end encryption compatible
* No database migrations needed

**Perfect for:**
* Surveys and feedback forms
* Quizzes and assessments
* Event registrations
* Expense declarations
* Data collection with privacy requirements

forum.description:
Create discussions, share ideas, and collaborate with your community directly in Nextcloud.

**Key features:**
- **Threaded Discussions** - Create and reply to organized discussion threads with pagination
- **Category Organization** - Structure your forum with customizable categories, headers, colors, and drag-and-drop reordering
- **Rich Text Formatting** - BBCode formatting with built-in and custom tags, toolbar with overflow menu
- **File Attachments** - Attach files from your Nextcloud storage or upload via drag-and-drop
- **Notifications** - Subscribe to threads and get notified on replies and @mentions
- **Post Reactions** - React to posts with emoji reactions
- **Read/Unread Tracking** - Track unread posts at thread and category level
- **Bookmarks** - Save threads for quick access
- **Search** - Advanced search with boolean operators and category filtering
- **User Profiles** - View post history, statistics, and role badges
- **Roles and Teams** - Fine-grained permissions per role or Nextcloud Team, per category
- **Guest Access** - Optional public access for unauthenticated visitors with configurable permissions
- **Edit History** - View post revision history with configurable visibility and per-account privacy controls
- **Reusable Templates** - Save and insert frequently used content snippets
- **Signatures** - BBCode-formatted signatures on posts
- **Thread Drafts** - Auto-saved drafts per category
- **Dashboard Widgets** - Recent activity, top threads, and top categories on the Nextcloud dashboard
- **Direct Post Links** - Link directly to a specific post within a thread
- **Moderation Tools** - Pin, lock, hide, and move threads; review and restore deleted content
- **Management Tools** - Manage categories, roles, BBCodes, and forum settings with granular permissions
- **Server Administration** - Repair seeds, rebuild statistics, and assign roles from the Nextcloud admin panel

**Perfect for:**
- Team discussions and collaboration
- Community forums
- Support channels
- Knowledge bases
- Project discussions
- Internal communication

The forum integrates seamlessly with your Nextcloud instance, using your existing accounts and teams for authentication and access control.

fulltextsearch_elasticsearch.description: Extension to the _Full text search_ app to communicate with ElasticSearch.

fulltextsearch_postgresql.description:
Full text search for Nextcloud without a search server: the index lives in the PostgreSQL
database your Nextcloud already uses.

PostgreSQL uses less memory and disk space, without sacrificing response time or search
quality.

- Indexing follows the language and folds accents, so "numerisation" finds "numérisation". The
  app takes the language of your instance, and can combine several.
- The app reads PDF and office files itself (docx, xlsx, pptx, odt, ods, odp), with no
  extraction service.
- Permissions are indexed with the content, so a search only returns documents the person
  running it can open.

Requires the Full text search app (fulltextsearch) and a content provider, usually the one for
files (files_fulltextsearch). The unaccent and pg_trgm extensions install themselves when the
database privileges allow; otherwise search stays accent-sensitive until an administrator
creates them.

geoblocker.description:
This is a front end to geo localization services, that allows blocking (beta), delaying (beta) and logging of login attempts from specified countries.
Login attempts from local network IP addresses are never blocked, delayed or logged.
In the current implementation the login page is normally shown to everybody independent of the country. Also login attempts with a non existing user are failing as usual independent of the country.
Wrong Nextcloud configuration (especially in container) can lead to all access seems to come from local network IP address.

integration_forgejo_gitea.description:
Bring the parts of Forgejo or Gitea that people actually check ten times a day into the Nextcloud dashboard. Signs in once with OAuth 2.0 authorization-code grant against your Forgejo or Gitea instance and then keeps the two systems talking in the background.

## Dashboard widgets

Eleven widgets, grouped by intent so the dashboard reads like your day rather than a list of API endpoints.

**Overview.** Six KPI tiles in a compact grid — open issues assigned, open issues you opened, open PRs where your review is requested, open PRs you opened, open issues mentioning you, contributions in the last 7 days. Each tile links to the equivalent Forgejo dashboard filter.

**Work queue.** Open Issues, Closed Issues, Open PRs, Closed PRs and Reviews. Each carries a per-widget repository picker (searchable multi-select), a filter (assigned / created / mentioning / all), and a refresh-frequency setting. Rows show number, title, assignee avatar, up to three colour-matched label chips, repo full-name and relative timestamp. A "Show all" link at the bottom of each widget lands on the equivalent Forgejo filter page.

**Activity.** Commits (latest commits across your selected repos, with an optional "only mine" toggle) and a GitHub-style contribution Heatmap (last 3 or 6 months, user-selectable) plus a stats grid showing total, this week, this month, current streak, longest streak, best day.

**Repositories.** Milestones (open milestones with progress bars across selected repos) and Repo stats (compact per-repo card showing stars, forks, open issues, open PRs, latest release tag).

**Notifications.** Unread Forgejo/Gitea notifications inbox with type icons (issue / PR / commit / repository) and a per-row mark-as-read action.

## Auto-refresh

All eleven widgets poll in the background at a user-selected cadence (Never / 30s / 1m / 5m default / 15m / 30m / 1h), pause while the browser tab is hidden, and re-fetch once when the tab regains focus. An idle dashboard tab left open in the background does not hammer your Forgejo.

## Brand-aware UX

Admin picks the instance type (Forgejo or Gitea). Every widget's icon and title switch to match — Forgejo orange horn (CC-BY-SA-4.0, Caesar Schinas), Gitea green tea-cup (CC-BY-4.0) — so a Nextcloud instance connected to Forgejo reads as *Forgejo: Open Issues*, a Gitea one reads *Gitea: Open Issues*.

## Security

OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow (RFC 6749) is the only connect path. 32-byte session-bound `state` parameter, verified with `hash_equals()`. Access and refresh tokens encrypted at rest via Nextcloud's `ICrypto`. Bearer tokens redacted from log messages. Generic error responses to the browser; upstream detail stays in the server log. Instance URL validated on admin write. Full OWASP Top 10 mapping in `SECURITY.md` in the repository.

## Requirements

Any recent Forgejo (v1.x, all v7+) or Gitea (v1.19+) instance with an OAuth application registered. PHP 8.1+, Nextcloud 30-34.

# Automatic Photo Album Creation for Nextcloud

Automatically cluster your images into journeys (vacations/trips) and create albums for each journey.
Only photos inside the timeline path you configured in Memories are used.
**Requires the Memories and Photos apps!**

> ### 🆕 New: Journals — your travel diary
> Keep a hand-written travel diary right inside Nextcloud. Create a Journal, add day entries (auto-filled with photos from that day), write your story, and curate the pictures. **Publish to a revocable public link** — a mobile-friendly timeline with locations, a route map, a visited countries & cities overview and a cover photo — or **share with other users and groups for full co-editing.** Find it in the new **Journeys** sidebar app.

## ✨ Features
- **🗺️ Location & Time Clustering:** Group images by when and where they were taken
- **🗂️ Album Creation:** Albums are created automatically for each journey
- **⚙️ Customizable:** Control minimum cluster size, time gap, and distance thresholds
- **🎥 Video Rendering:** Turn journey albums into MP4 highlight reels. Renders run as background jobs (the settings page returns instantly) and land in `Documents/Journeys Movies/`. Per-location subtitles fade in/out as the journey moves between places. Requires `ffmpeg` on the server.
- **📔 Journals (travel diary):** Keep a hand-written travel diary in the new **Journeys** sidebar app: create a Journal, add a day entry (auto-filled with up to 20 photos spread across that day), write text, curate the photos and add a caption to each. Photos stay in capture-time order, so pictures added by a collaborator merge into the day's timeline where they were actually taken. Publish a Journal to a revocable public link — a mobile-friendly timeline with locations, a visited countries/cities overview and a cover photo. Share a Journal with other users or groups for full co-editing — and each member can optionally let the others pick from their own photo library for the journal's dates. Mark a Journal as completed when you're home; it then shows its travel stats — days, countries, distance travelled and photo count. Give a Journal a description and it appears under the title, in the list and on the shared page. When adding a day, a month calendar highlights the days that actually hold photos. Automatic nightly clustering is opt-in: the app asks once, and a switch in personal settings turns it on or off at any time.
- **📚 Mobile-friendly journey browser:** Compact card list with year, month and location filters plus a `▶ Watch` shortcut to existing rendered videos — built for instances with many journeys.
- **🧵 Smart Merging:** Adjacent clusters in the same country (within one week) are automatically stitched together, so multi-city road trips and long vacations with rest days stay as one journey
- **🧹 Auto-cleanup of empty albums:** Journey albums whose photos you've all deleted are removed automatically on the next clustering run, so empty placeholders don't pile up. Manual albums are never touched.
- **✏️ User-editable journey names:** Set a custom name (e.g. *Christmas 2024*, *Family reunion*, *Sabbatical*) on top of the auto-derived location/date title. Custom names become the card heading, the Photos album title, and the video title overlay — and they survive `--from-scratch` reclustering by matching old names to new clusters via file-ID overlap.

## 🚀 OCC Command Usage

    php occ journeys:cluster-create-albums <user>

## 🏠 Using your home location (default)
Journeys segments the timeline into **near home** and **away from home** and applies sensible defaults for each to capture local days vs. trips.

## ⏰ Runs automatically
A background job runs **daily** to cluster newly added photos, and you’ll receive a **notification** whenever new albums are created.

## 🏷️ How album names are created
Album titles are generated from the **resolved place name** and the **date range** of the cluster, e.g. `Iceland — Aug 12–19, 2024`.

ktec_talkbot.description:
**Talk-Bot** turns any Nextcloud Talk conversation into an AI chat.

Enable the app, put your API key in the admin settings, and switch the bot on in a
conversation — that is the whole setup. No external daemon, no webhook endpoint,
no Docker image and no separate machine are required: the bot runs entirely inside
Nextcloud as a Talk in-app bot, in a few hundred kilobytes of PHP.

### Light by design

One small app, installed from the App Store like any other. There is nothing else
to run and nothing else to keep alive. It answers off the request path, so posting
a message never waits for the model.

### Bring your own model — or your own subscription

- **Native and OpenAI-compatible.** Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini through
  their own APIs, plus **any OpenAI-compatible endpoint**: OpenRouter, DeepSeek,
  Qwen/DashScope, Mistral, Groq, OpenAI itself, or a local server such as Ollama,
  vLLM or LM Studio.
- **Use a CLI subscription instead of API tokens.** If a Claude or Gemini command
  line tool is installed on the server, the bot can drive it — so a flat-rate
  subscription answers your users, with no per-token API bill. Off by default.
- **Pick the model from a list.** The settings page fetches the models your key
  can actually use, so there is nothing to type by hand, and only one place to set
  it. A connection test confirms it answers before your users try it.

### Two tiers: an assistant for everyone, maintenance for admins

- **Ordinary users get a sandbox.** No tools, no files, no shell, no way to touch
  the server — just a helpful assistant that answers questions.
- **Administrators can get real access, only if you turn it on.** A request is
  treated as elevated only when three things are all true: the sender is in the
  Nextcloud **admin group**, the **command line** engine is selected, and the
  **Tools for Nextcloud administrators** field is set. Because it keys off
  Nextcloud's own admin group, this follows your existing roles automatically —
  there is no separate "bot admin" list to maintain.

When elevated, the bot runs the command line tool **with the rights of the account
Nextcloud runs as** (its web server / PHP process user, whose name varies by
system), so an admin can inspect logs, read and change configuration, edit files
and run commands, straight from a Talk conversation.
That is not root, but it is still broad — every member of the admin group shares
it and it fires from an ordinary chat message, so enable it deliberately. Set
`default` for all tools, or a short list such as `Bash,Read,Edit`; clear the
field and admins drop back to the sandbox. The user and admin tiers are two
separate, independently-set lists, and **both are empty by default**. Anyone can
send `?whoami` to see their own tier.

### And the rest

- **Per-conversation memory.** Each user keeps their own history in every room;
  `?reset` starts over. Commands: `?help`, `?reset`, `?status`, `?whoami`.
- **Access control.** Optionally restrict the bot to an allow-list of users.
- **Reply language.** Answer always in a fixed language, or mirror the user.

### Privacy

Messages sent to the bot go to the AI provider you configure, and nowhere else.
API keys are stored encrypted in the Nextcloud configuration and are never sent
back to the browser. Point the bot at a local model server and nothing leaves your
machine at all.

Requires the Nextcloud Talk app.

**Learning** is a self-hosted learning platform for Nextcloud. Your questions, progress, and student data never leave your server.

Built for IT certification bootcamps (CompTIA, Cisco, AWS) but works for any subject. Instructors create courses, track student progress, and identify at-risk learners. Students drill with scientifically-backed spaced repetition and hands-on simulations.

## Why Learning?

- **Your data stays on your server** — no cloud dependency, full GDPR compliance
- **FSRS adaptive scheduling** — cards are prioritized by memory strength, not rigid intervals
- **9 interactive IT simulators** — CLI terminals, firewall builders, DNS resolvers, subnet calculators, network topology placement
- **AI tutor (optional)** — answers questions by citing your uploaded course materials
- **Verifiable certificates** — issue cryptographically signed, publicly verifiable completion credentials

## For Instructors

- Course management with pool assignment and student enrollment
- **At-risk warnings** — automatic detection of struggling students
- **Chapter heatmaps** — see where the class struggles at a glance
- **Curriculum timeline** — plan course schedule with milestones
- **Admin dashboard** — CSV export, course archiving, cohort merging
- Campaign selection — choose which story scenarios are available per course

## Certification & Compliance

- **Signed completion certificates** — every passing learner receives a cryptographically signed (Ed25519) certificate, minted automatically
- **Public verification portal** — anyone can verify a certificate's authenticity via its permanent URL, no login required
- **Compliance reports** — organization-wide completion overview for audits and works agreements
- **Mandatory training & recertification** — assign required courses, track certificate expiry, and automate recertification reminders
- **Tamper-proof audit trail** — every issuance, revocation, and completion is logged

## For Learners

- **Smart Queue** — one-click review of all due cards, sorted by urgency
- **Training & Exam Mode** — practice or simulate timed exams
- **PBQ Simulations** — performance-based questions with interactive CLI, drag-and-drop placement, and wiring tasks
- **Story Campaigns** — learn through real IT incident scenarios (WannaCry, SolarWinds, Log4Shell)
- **Live Duels & Sprint** — real-time multiplayer quiz battles via Server-Sent Events
- **Gamification** — XP, levels, streaks, 10 badges, seasonal league
- **Maintenance Mode** — long-term retention schedule after course ends
- **Trouble-spot cheat sheet** — export your weakest topics for exam prep

## AI Features (optional)

Requires a Google Gemini API key. Without it, the app is fully functional — AI features are simply hidden. Each user must explicitly opt in before any data is sent to the API.

- **VirtuProf** — AI learning assistant with RAG-powered answers and source citations
- **Question Generator** — create flashcards from pasted text
- **Note Generator** — AI-powered topic summaries saved to Nextcloud Files

## Question Types

- Multiple Choice, Free Text with fuzzy matching, PBQ Simulations
- CSV/JSON import & export, pool sharing, multi-language translations

## Technical

- Vue 3, Vite, Pinia — modern frontend stack
- 1220 unit tests, PHPStan Level 5, pre-push quality gates
- Native Nextcloud integration: Dashboard widgets, Notifications, Talk, Files
- AGPL-3.0 — fully open source

## Requirements

- Nextcloud 33–35
- PHP 8.1+
- PostgreSQL 13+ or MySQL 8+

**Looking for pilot partners!** If you run Nextcloud at a school, university, or training provider — we'd love your feedback. Open an issue with a bit of context and we're happy to walk you through it.

llmchat.description:
**Privacy-first by architecture. Batteries included. Bring your own LLM.**

A chat interface for large language models where **your browser talks directly to the LLM backend**.
Nextcloud acts only as configuration storage and archive target — it is never a proxy and never sees
prompts or responses. Not "we promise not to look": it structurally cannot.

Because the requests originate in the browser, `localhost` resolves from the *user's* machine. Your
Nextcloud can live in a datacenter and still talk to an Ollama instance running on your laptop —
no tunnel, no VPN, no exposed port. No server-side LLM app can do that.

Features:

* Bring your own backend: Ollama, llama.cpp, LiteLLM, OpenRouter, vLLM — anything OpenAI-compatible
* Multiple connections with encrypted API key storage, multiple profiles per connection
* Profiles carry model, system prompt, temperature, token budget, streaming and reasoning switches
* Streaming responses with a stop button, edit-and-retry, regenerate — including regenerating the
  same question with a different profile or model
* Full-text search across your local chat history
* Optional agent tools: web search via your own SearXNG, page fetching, clock, and read-only
  access to your own Nextcloud (Unified Search, Collectives, files, PDF text) — no MCP server,
  no extra container, no app password needed
* Skills: Markdown files in your own Files where you write down how a kind of question should be
  answered, which source to use and how the reply should look. Ships with a weather example that
  replaces a web search with one API call, fetched by your browser from a host you allowlisted
* Models can ask you a question in a dialog instead of guessing at an ambiguous requirement
* File picker in the composer, so a path goes into the prompt without being typed
* "LLM Chat" in the Files menu opens a new chat with that file's path already in the prompt
* Vision-capable models can be shown an image or a rendered PDF page from your files, behind a
  per-profile switch that is off by default
* Approval dialog before any tool call that leaves the browser, on by default
* Chat history in IndexedDB — local to the browser, by design
* Archive chats as Markdown files into your Nextcloud files
* Profile export/import as JSON (never contains secrets)

**Note:** API keys are stored encrypted on the server but are necessarily delivered to the browser,
since that is where the request is made. Each user only ever sees their own key.

# Know what is due. Close it in the field.

MaintenanceCheck runs recurring and corrective maintenance on the Nextcloud you already host. Put customers, sites and equipment in one register. Schedule by calendar or meter. Turn due visits into work orders with checklists, photos and optional signatures — then hand the office a Servicebericht PDF.

**Free web app** (AGPL-3.0-or-later). Companion apps: https://nextcloud.software-by-design.de/

## Why teams install it

- **See overdue work first** — due board for overdue, today, next 7 days and the weeks ahead, plus open jobs

## Clear limits

- Customers here are a field register. Same name in another business app ≠ same record; nothing merges on its own.
- Optional stock deduction after close stays off by default and never blocks finishing a job.

## Feedback welcome

## 🚀 Installation

moodle_talk_bridge.description:
Connect your Moodle courses to Nextcloud Talk. A teacher adds a **Nextcloud
Talk Session** to a course, and everything else happens on its own: the
conversation is created, the class is added to it, and everyone joins with a
single click. No extra logins, no manual room admin.

**What your users get**

- **One click into the meeting.** Teachers and students open the activity in
  Moodle and land in the Talk conversation already signed in. There is no
  second password to remember.
- **Accounts created for them.** Course participants who do not yet have a
  Nextcloud account get one automatically the first time they join.
- **The right people, with the right rights.** Teachers become moderators,
  students join as participants, and membership follows course enrolment — so
  the room stays correct as the class changes.
- **Rooms that follow the course.** A conversation is created when the
  activity is added, renamed when the activity is renamed, and archived when
  it is removed.
- **Private by design.** Every exchange between Moodle and Nextcloud is signed
  and verified, and only the Moodle sites you approve are accepted.

**Setting it up**

Everything is configured in your browser. No command line and no server access
are required.

1. Make sure **Nextcloud Talk** is installed and enabled.
2. Install this app from **Apps → Integration**.
3. Open **Administration settings → Moodle Talk Bridge** and complete the six

**Plan projects the way project managers actually work — inside your own Nextcloud.**

Gantt Projects manages projects, subprojects, tasks and milestones in an interactive Gantt chart with a synced table view. Scheduling, resources, baselines and reporting run entirely on your instance: no external service, no tracking, no data leaving your server.

## ✨ Features

* 📊 **Gantt chart & table view**: Day, week, month and sprint scale with milestone diamonds, progress bars, today line and weekend shading. The table on the left shows exactly the same rows and offers configurable columns, inline editing and full keyboard navigation. Projects, subprojects and tasks can be collapsed, and subprojects and tasks can carry their own colour or inherit it from their parent.
* 🔗 **Dependencies & scheduling**: n:m dependencies of all four types (FS, SS, FF, SF) with lag and lead time in working days — set per dependency in the task dialog or typed in MS-Project notation (`12FS+2d`) in the table. Moves propagate through the whole chain and cycles are rejected.
* 🎯 **Critical path**: Forward and backward pass with float computed on the server; the chain that really drives the end date is highlighted in the chart.
* 📈 **Earned Value Management**: PV, EV, AC, SPI and CPI next to rollup KPIs for progress, effort, budget and risk.
* 📐 **Baselines & delta report**: Freeze a plan, keep it visible as a second bar, and compare the current schedule against it element by element.
* 🔮 **What-if simulation**: Play through date shifts without touching the saved plan — ghost bars keep the real dates in view.
* 👥 **Resources & capacity**: Resource groups, resources optionally linked to a Nextcloud user account, multiple assignees per task with individual effort shares, a day-level capacity grid, a workload chart below the timeline and over-allocation warnings.
* 📅 **Working calendars**: Week models, regional calendars and holidays — every date calculation in the app counts working days accordingly.
* 🤝 **Sharing & permissions**: Share individual projects with other users as viewer, editor or project admin; the interface hides what a role may not do.
* 🗓️ **Calendar feed (ICS)**: Subscribe to project dates and milestones in Thunderbird, Nextcloud Calendar or a mobile app via a per-project token that can be revoked at any time — or subscribe to a personal feed with just your own tasks and milestones across all projects. Optionally, your tasks are also written as to-dos into the Nextcloud Tasks app (one-way).
* 🔄 **Import & export**: JSON including resources, capacities and working calendars, CSV for spreadsheets, and the rendered chart as PNG, SVG or PDF.
* 🃏 **Deck integration**: Link projects, subprojects and tasks to a Nextcloud Deck board, its lists and cards as a cross-reference and take a task's progress from its card (done or share of the checklist). Nothing is written to Deck yet — the [integration overview](https://codeberg.org/fds2610/NC-Gantt/src/branch/main/nc_gantt/docs/en/FEATURES.md#integrations-at-a-glance) shows what flows where.
* 🏠 **Dashboard widgets**: A compact Gantt of your active projects and your next due or overdue tasks — each one a click away — right on the Nextcloud dashboard.
* 🔔 **Notifications**: A daily background job sends a Nextcloud notification for tasks and milestones that are due today, due soon or overdue — to the accounts linked to the assigned resources, or to the project owner when no link exists. Each project sets its own lead time in working days, whether it reminds about milestones only and whether overdue items are included; everyone can mute the notifications in their personal settings. On top of the daily run, changes are reported as they happen: a new assignment, and dates that have moved — those arising from the dependency chain too, bundled into one message per person and never about your own change.
* ↩️ **Undo & audit log**: Take back an accidental move including its propagation chain; field changes are recorded.
* 🔍 **Search & filters**: Find items by title or filter by risk, overdue, over budget, resource, tasks assigned to you or missing Deck link — without losing the time context.
* 📖 **Glossary**: Around 30 project-management terms with their formulas, built right into the app.
* 🌐 **Localisation**: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Brazilian Portuguese.

Requires Nextcloud 31–35 and PHP 8.1 or newer. Works with MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL and SQLite.

## 📚 Documentation

* 🚀 [HOWTO](https://codeberg.org/fds2610/NC-Gantt/src/branch/main/nc_gantt/docs/en/HOWTO.md) — plan a sample project step by step, from the working calendar to the finished report
* 📋 [Feature reference](https://codeberg.org/fds2610/NC-Gantt/src/branch/main/nc_gantt/docs/en/FEATURES.md) — every function with its purpose, input and output
* 📝 [Changelog](https://codeberg.org/fds2610/NC-Gantt/src/branch/main/nc_gantt/CHANGELOG.md) — what changed in each release
* 💾 [Installation](https://codeberg.org/fds2610/NC-Gantt/src/branch/main/nc_gantt/docs/en/INSTALL.md) — setup and update notes

## 🐛 Feedback

Bug reports and feature requests are welcome in the [issue tracker](https://codeberg.org/fds2610/NC-Gantt/issues).

netbase.description:
NetBase turns your Nextcloud into a network console: it finds every device on the LAN, opens each one's own settings page from inside Nextcloud, and keeps the everyday lookup tools on the same screen.

Device windows are the heart of it. The server fetches a device's own web interface and rewrites every address inside it, so a router, a switch, a printer or a NAS can be signed into and configured from anywhere the Nextcloud is reachable — no VPN, no jump host, no site visit. Firmware can be sent, a configuration restored, a backup taken. Several windows can be open at once.

Discovery needs no root, no agent and no extra packages: NetBase primes the kernel neighbour table, reads it back, and asks each device for its own name over NetBIOS, mDNS, WS-Discovery and SSDP. It also listens for the announcements devices make, continuously and in the background, so a device sitting on another subnet of the same wire — one nothing here can reach, and which can never answer a question — still appears in the list. MAC addresses are resolved against a bundled IEEE registry of more than 53,000 vendor prefixes, offline.

What each part is for:
- Device windows — a device's own settings page, through Nextcloud, from anywhere
- LAN sweep and inventory — name, IPv4, MAC, vendor, type and open ports, exportable as CSV
- DNS — any record type from any resolver, resolver comparison, delegation trace, zone-transfer test
- Whois and free-domain search — look up any domain or address (IANA referrals, no whois binary), or check a name across a whole range of endings at once to find one that is still free
- Wake-on-LAN — wake a device by its MAC address
- TLS and HTTP — certificate, chain and expiry, accepted TLS versions, redirect chain, security headers
- Mail — SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS, DANE and blocklists, plus SMTP/IMAP/POP3 server tests, an open-relay test and a real test message
- FTP and SFTP — browse a remote server and move files to and from your Nextcloud folders
- SSH and Telnet — a credential-free probe, and commands or a full terminal on a saved connection
- Benchmarks — internet speed, LAN throughput over iperf3, resolver comparison, HTTP timing
- Every result can be copied, downloaded or saved straight into your own Nextcloud files

Access is per tool. NetBase is an administrator's app, and everything that touches the local network defaults to administrators — but each tool can be opened to named groups or to everyone from Administration settings, so an instance can lend out whois, DNS and the other harmless lookups without lending out the network. Where an account is allowed nothing, NetBase leaves itself out of that account's app menu.

Available in twenty languages, and NetBase can be set to a different language from the rest of Nextcloud, per account.

NoteBerg is a note-taking app combining handwriting, rich text, and Nextcloud sync.

## Features

### Handwriting & Drawing

- Lasso selection — move, resize, rotate, copy selected strokes
- Eraser tool, unlimited undo/redo
- Mark handwritten notes as tasks

### Text Editing
- Rich text editor (WYSIWYG) with formatting, tables, colors, and font sizes
- Automatic mode switching between drawing and text editing
- Task checkboxes inline with notes

### Media & Import/Export
- PDF import — annotate PDFs with pen and text
- Image insertion with cropping and perspective correction
- PDF export with automatic A4 pagination

### Organization
- Notebooks for hierarchical organization
- Note overview with thumbnail previews
- Full-text search across handwriting and typed text
- Markers tab — browse task markers across all notes
- Recycle bin with soft delete and permanent deletion

### Sync & Storage
- Offline-first — all data stored locally in IndexedDB
- Nextcloud sync via WebDAV with conflict resolution

### UI
- Dark mode / light mode with system preference detection
- Background patterns — ruled lines and grid
- Internationalization — English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Chinese

### Handwriting Recognition
- Optional AI recognition with a vision model you configure yourself — off by default, always started manually.
- Nothing is sent anywhere unless you turn it on and supply your own provider details.
- When you start a recognition, your handwriting is rendered as an image and sent from your Nextcloud server to the endpoint you configured, and the transcribed text is returned.
- The request is made by the server rather than the browser, so your API key stays on the server and is never exposed to the web page. It is stored encrypted.

### AI Integration (optional)
- A shared, off-by-default AI provider connection (endpoint, model, API key) configured once per account in the app's settings. There is no built-in or shared service, and no key ships with the app.
- AI handwriting recognition (above) is the first feature built on this connection, with more planned.

### Data & Privacy
- All note data is stored exclusively on your own Nextcloud server — no third-party services or telemetry, except for the optional AI recognition described above, which is off unless you configure it
- Note: uninstalling this app does not delete your note data from the server. Your notes remain in the /NoteBerg/ WebDAV folder and can be re-accessed by reinstalling the app. This is intentional — your data may also have been synced there by the NoteBerg desktop or mobile app.

### Also available on other platforms
- Android: native app via Google Play open testing: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=eu.noteberg.app
- Windows: desktop installer from GitHub Releases: https://github.com/thomasleuthold/NoteBerg/releases (unsigned build; Windows may warn about an unknown publisher)
