paperless_sync.description:
### A native bridge between Paperless-ngx and Nextcloud

Paperless Sync mirrors finalized Paperless-ngx documents into a readable Nextcloud folder structure. Paperless remains the authoritative document archive while Nextcloud provides familiar access through Files, desktop sync, mobile apps, sharing, and its built-in viewer.

### Structured, automatic, and reversible

- Exports archive PDFs or original files through the Paperless API
- Builds a configurable hierarchy from correspondent, document type, date, title, and document ID
- Moves or renames files when Paperless metadata changes
- Skips Paperless inbox documents until they are finalized and removes previously mirrored copies when an exclusion tag is added
- Imports files from a configurable Nextcloud inbox into Paperless
- Mirrors the Paperless trash into a dedicated Nextcloud folder
- Optionally removes files after they are permanently deleted from Paperless
- Removes empty archive folders after moves and deletions
- Runs through native Nextcloud background jobs with resumable state

### Safe by default

Synchronization is disabled until an administrator completes and validates the configuration. Permanent deletion is an explicit opt-in and can be protected by multiple missing-document confirmations. A dry-run previews changes without modifying files.

The Paperless API token is stored server-side in Nextcloud's credentials manager and is never returned to the browser. The app operates directly through Nextcloud's filesystem API, so no Nextcloud password or WebDAV credential is required.

### Requirements

- Nextcloud 33 to 35 with reliable cron background jobs
- A reachable Paperless-ngx instance with API access
- A dedicated Paperless service account with only the permissions needed for the enabled features

Paperless Sync is independent from [Paperless Unified Search](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/paperless_unified_search). Both apps understand stable document markers such as `[P123]` and can be installed separately.

paperless_unified_search.description:
### Paperless search, seamlessly integrated into Nextcloud

Paperless Unified Search brings Paperless-ngx's OCR-powered document search directly into Nextcloud's global search. Find invoices, contracts, letters, statements, and any text recognized inside your documents — without leaving Nextcloud.

### Search in Paperless. Work in Nextcloud.

- Uses Paperless-ngx's native OCR and full-text search
- Shows results directly in Nextcloud's global search
- Opens the synchronized file in Nextcloud's built-in viewer on web, iOS, and Android
- Matches documents through stable markers such as `[P123]`
- Includes only files the current Nextcloud user is allowed to access
- Automatically excludes documents that have not yet been synchronized

### Privacy and access control

Paperless is queried server-to-server. The API token is stored in Nextcloud's encrypted credentials manager and is never exposed to the browser.

By default, searches are sent to Paperless only when users enable connected-services search. Administrators can optionally mark their Paperless server as trusted and include it automatically in every global search.

A dedicated, read-only Paperless account is recommended.

### Requirements

- Nextcloud 33 to 35
- A reachable Paperless-ngx instance with API access
- Synchronized files whose names contain their Paperless document marker, for example `[P123]`

This app provides search integration only. It does not synchronize documents between Paperless and Nextcloud.

### Native synchronization companion

For structured document synchronization, use the independent [Paperless Sync](https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-sync) Nextcloud app. Both apps use the same stable `[P123]` document marker and can be maintained and updated separately.

# PhoneTrack Nextcloud application

📱 PhoneTrack is a Nextcloud application to track and store mobile device's locations.

🗺 It receives information from mobile phone's logging apps and displays it dynamically on a map.

🌍 Help us to translate this app on [PhoneTrack Crowdin project](https://crowdin.com/project/phonetrack).

⚒ Check out other ways to help in the [contribution guidelines](https://gitlab.com/eneiluj/phonetrack-oc/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).

How to use PhoneTrack :

- Create a tracking session.
- Give the logging link\* to the mobile devices. Choose the [logging method](https://github.com/julien-nc/phonetrack/blob/main/doc/user.md#logging-methods) you prefer.
- Watch the session's devices location in real time (or not) in PhoneTrack or share it with public pages.

(\*) Don't forget to set the device name in the link (rather than in the logging app settings). Replace "yourname" with the desired device name.
Setting the device name in logging app settings only works with Owntracks, Traccar and OpenGTS.

On PhoneTrack main page, while watching a session, you can :

- 📍 Display location history
- ⛛ Filter points
- ✎ Manually edit/add/delete points
- ✎ Edit devices (rename, change colour/shape, move to another session)
- ⛶ Define geofencing zones for devices
- ⚇ Define proximity alerts for device pairs
- 🖧 Share a session to other Nextcloud users or with a public link (read-only)
- 🔗 Generate public share links with optional restrictions (filters, device name, last positions only, geofencing simplification)
- 🖫 Import/export a session in GPX format (one file with one track per device or one file per device)
- 🗠 Display sessions statistics
- 🔒 [Reserve a device name](https://github.com/julien-nc/phonetrack/blob/main/doc/user.md#device-name-reservation) to make sure only authorized user can log with this name
- 🗓 Toggle session auto export and auto purge (daily/weekly/monthly)
- ◔ Choose what to do when point number quota is reached (block logging or delete oldest point)

Public page and public filtered page work like main page except there is only one session displayed, everything is read-only and there is no need to be logged in.

This app is under development.

previewgenerator.description:
The Preview Generator app allows admins to pre-generate previews. The app listens to edit events and stores this information. Once a cron job is triggered it will generate start preview generation. This means that you can better utilize your system by pre-generating previews when your system is normally idle and thus putting less load on your machine when the requests are actually served.

The app does not replace on demand preview generation so if a preview is requested before it is pre-generated it will still be shown.
The first time you install this app, before using a cron job, you properly want to generate all previews via:
**occ preview:generate-all -vvv**

The preview queue will be processed automatically by a background job if the system cron background job mode is configured in Nextcloud. Additionally, you may run **occ preview:pre-generate -vvv** to a process the queue of pending previews immediately.

**This app has to be installed and used together with the [Nextcloud Office](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/richdocuments) integration app.**

Collabora Online is a powerful LibreOffice-based online office suite with collaborative editing, which supports all major documents, spreadsheet and presentation file formats and works together with all modern browsers.

* This app provides a built-in server with all of the document editing features of Collabora Online.
* Easy to install, for personal use or for small teams.
* A bit slower than a standalone server and without the advanced scalability features.

**System Requirements:**
- Linux running on ```x86-64``` or ```arm64/aarch64```
- A ```glibc``` based distribution/container (```musl libc``` is **not** supported)
- Fontconfig (```libfontconfig.so.1```)
- Additional requirements can be found in [here](https://github.com/CollaboraOnline/richdocumentscode#richdocumentscode)

*The download is rather big so it is possible you will experience a time-out when installing via the web interface.* You can use the OCC command install the built-in server from the command-line instead:

```
sudo -u wwwrun php -d memory_limit=512M ./occ app:install richdocumentscode
```
Where `wwwrun` is the user of your web server. This is ```www-data``` on Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives, `wwwrun` on SUSE based distributions, `apache` on Red Hat/Fedora and `http` on Arch linux and derivatives.

Updates can be done like this:
```
sudo -u wwwrun php -d memory_limit=512M ./occ app:update --all
```

Of course, alternatively you could increase memory usage and PHP time-outs by default, see the [Nextcloud documentation.](https://docs.nextcloud.com/server/latest/admin_manual/configuration_files/big_file_upload_configuration.html?highlight=php%20timeout#configuring-your-web-server)

s3_api.description:
**Point any S3 client at a Nextcloud folder.**

Mark a folder as a bucket in your personal settings, create an API key, and use it with the AWS
CLI, boto3, rclone or any other S3-compatible client. The files stay ordinary Nextcloud files —
visible in the web UI, synced by the desktop client, shareable, versioned. Nothing is duplicated
into a separate object store.

Rather than the handful of calls a file sync needs, this implements the parts that make an S3
endpoint usable as a real backend:

* Conditional writes (`If-Match` / `If-None-Match`) that serialise concurrent writers, so the
  store works as a compare-and-swap primitive
* Multipart uploads, including `UploadPartCopy` for server-side compose
* Ranged and conditional reads, delimited listings, presigned URLs
* Streaming uploads — bodies are never buffered in memory, and `aws-chunked` payloads have their
  per-chunk signature chain verified
* Correct S3 ETags (content MD5, compound form for multipart) rather than Nextcloud's internal
  etag, which is too coarse to build a compare-and-swap on

Authentication is AWS Signature V4, via header or presigned URL. Each API key is scoped to exactly
one bucket and is either readonly or readwrite.

Verified against [walgit](https://github.com/tobi/walgit)'s store contract suite, which exercises
compare-and-swap under 32-way concurrency, ranged reads, delimited listings and multipart round
trips.

**Note:** every request passes through PHP and Nextcloud's storage layer. This is a convenient way
to talk S3 to data you already keep in Nextcloud — not a replacement for a high-throughput object
store.

## Print from Nextcloud to SavaPage

Send documents directly from Nextcloud to a [SavaPage](https://www.savapage.org) print server.

- Send a **single file** from the Files app context menu.
- **Batch print** multiple files or whole folders; folders are expanded recursively on the server.
- Allowed file types are enforced server-side, so only printable documents are sent.
- Credentials are managed per user and can be synced automatically from SavaPage, or overridden by users when the administrator allows it.
- Dedicated **SavaPage** sections in both Administration and Personal settings.

### Requirements

- Nextcloud 28 – 34
- PHP 8.2+
- A reachable SavaPage server

### Installation

Install SavaPage Print from the [Nextcloud App Store](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/savapage), or download a release archive and enable it in your `apps` directory.

### How it works

When you choose *Print to SavaPage*, the app uploads the document to your SavaPage server (`{Server URI}/restful/v1/documents/print`) using your personal SavaPage ID and UUID. SavaPage then holds the document in its print queue for you to release at the printer.

[Read the full documentation](https://www.savapage.org) for administrator and user guides.

scoreview.description:
ScoreView displays MuseScore scores (.mscz) directly from Files - as faithful
MuseScore notation (SVG) with a playback cursor that follows client-side
synthesized MIDI playback in sync, instead of a static PDF export.

Made for choir and ensemble work: the notation looks like the sheet music you
already know, every voice can be heard on its own, and every measure is one
click away.

An uploaded .mscz file is converted once, server-side, to notation pages (SVG),
MIDI and timing data, then cached: opening the same file again does not
re-render, it is served from the cache. Only a change to the file triggers a
new conversion.

There are two equivalent conversion paths that produce the same result. The
default one needs no configuration at all and no container: MuseScore as
WebAssembly, executed by the server's Node.js runtime - everything it needs
ships with the app, and the server fetches the SoundFont for playback on its
own. Alternatively a MuseScore container next to Nextcloud does the
converting.

Feature set: zoom presets, fullscreen and auto-scrolling in time with playback;
a freely configurable playback highlight (sounding notes or a bar, in a colour
of your choice);
measure navigation, looping over a measure range, click-to-note jump and
keyboard shortcuts; a mixer with per-voice volume/mute/solo, a "my voice"
preset, tempo in BPM and a metronome; annotations anchored to musical
position (private or shared, surviving a re-upload); touch controls with
pinch-zoom for a tablet on the music stand.

secrets.description:
Secrets allows users to generate share links for text based data (e.g. passwords, CSV lists, bank accounts...) that can be sent to anyone (including receivers without a Nextcloud account) for retrieval. The data itself will be end-to-end encrypted (so not even Nextcloud can access it) and the encryption key will be part of the share link (the anchor part) - but never be actually sent to the server. Once retrieved, the secret will be deleted from the server, ensuring, that if it arrived at the correct receiver it has been seen by nobody else.

Secrets now comes with a cli that can be used to automate the provisioning of secret shares: https://github.com/theCalcaholic/nextcloud-secrets/releases

social.description:
Nextcloud Social connects your Nextcloud account to the Fediverse through the ActivityPub standard.

What it does:
- 🧭 Timelines: home, local, global (federated), direct messages, liked posts, notifications, hashtags
- ✍️ Posts: write posts and replies with a visibility setting, mentions, hashtags, content warnings and media attachments
- ✏️ Edit and delete your own posts; edits are federated as ActivityPub Update activities
- 👍 🔁 💬 Like, boost and reply
- 👥 Follow and unfollow local and remote accounts; incoming follows are accepted automatically unless the account is locked
- 🔎 Find accounts and hashtags via WebFinger and search
- 🌐 Federation: signed delivery of ActivityPub activities, with a delivery queue processed by cron
- 📊 Dashboard tiles for mentions, direct messages, your timeline, bookmarks, follow requests and trending hashtags, plus open reports and federation health for administrators
- 🔒 Photos have their Exif metadata — including the coordinates a phone writes into them — removed before they are stored or federated
- 🎬 A Videos timeline, including the videos from PeerTube channels anyone here follows: streamed from the instance that holds them rather than copied here, and proxied so no viewer's address reaches a server they never chose
- 📡 Videos posted here federate as ActivityPub Video objects filed under a channel, which is what PeerTube needs before it will take one at all, with a poster frame, byte-range seeking and a 2 GB ceiling of their own
- ▶️ A video opens on a watch page: its title, the channel with a Subscribe button, its chapters as links that seek, and where you stopped offered back as continue watching. Every channel and account has an RSS feed with an enclosure per video
- 🪜 An administrator can have each stored video written at a ladder of smaller sizes as HLS, so a player picks what the connection carries; and can set a per-account video quota, see who is holding the disk, choose what happens to media marked sensitive, and hold every post with a video for a moderator
- 📥 A channel can be brought over from PeerTube's own export, or a single video by its address
- 🎨 Filters in the composer and a profile that draws as a grid
- 🗂️ Collections, stories and places
- 📱 Pixelfed's own routes — the config its app reads on launch, discover, the story carousel, collections, mutuals, reports, direct-message threads, push (honestly off) and its admin screens — so its app finds what it looks for once the API is at the domain root
- 🖼️ Stories, collections and places in the web app: a row of faces above your feed with a player and a way to post one; albums as the fourth tab of a profile, each a page of its posts; a pin in the composer that says where a picture was taken, and a page for every place — with nothing ever sent to a map service
- 🧭 A Discover page: who to follow, with starter packs you can follow in one go
- 📤 Share to Social from the Files app: pick pictures or videos there and the composer opens with them attached
- 👥 Lists, and every Nextcloud group you are in as a list of its own — kept in step with the group automatically; you make, rename, delete and fill your own in Settings
- ⚙️ Account settings: the name you publish under, whether people ask before they follow you, whether other servers may suggest you and index your public posts, and the audience every new post starts with
- 🔗 The profile editor says which of your fields are verified links, and gives you the line to paste on your own site to earn the tick
- 👋 A short introduction on the first visit: your address, who to follow, and a way to bring the follows you already have
- 📱 A layout for phones: the post takes the width of the screen, the face inside the card, the composer's toolbar wrapping
- 🔗 Links that land where they should: a post or profile link opens inside the app when you are signed in, a search can be reloaded or sent to somebody, and an address that names nobody says so instead of erroring
- 🩺 For administrators: four setup checks in Administration → Overview — WebFinger, the address ids are built from, the delivery job and the outbound queue — and a Server card for the instance settings that used to need occ
- 🔗 A link to a post or a profile here unfurls into a card in Talk, Text and Deck
- 🕘 Follows, mentions, boosts and favourites show in the Activity app too, and in its digest mail for those who turn that on
- 🗓️ A composer that says what a post is: the language it is written in, a clock to publish it later (with the waiting posts listed in Settings), and a crosshair that says where the subject of a picture is
- 😀 Emoji reactions on a post, federated as EmojiReact, with the faces behind each one
- 💬 Quote posts, carrying the original author's permission on the wire
- 😀 Custom emoji of this instance's own, added with occ social:emoji and rendered on servers that have never seen them
- 🎞️ A GIF picker in the composer, backed by the instance's own library rather than a third party
- 📈 Your own statistics: the last 30 days beside the 30 before them — reach, interactions, likes and boosts, each with the percentage it moved by — then every post of the window one by one, what works, when to post and where your followers are. A statistics page for the instance too, and profile highlights showing what somebody posts about
- 🕰️ On this day, and a weekly recap of what you missed
- 📣 Announcements: what the administrators of this instance are telling everybody, at the top of the timeline until it is read, dismissed once for every device, with an emoji to say something back
- 📡 Relays: subscribe to one and a new server's federated timeline stops being empty — a relay rebroadcasts the public posts of every server on it and carries this server's public posts out to all of them. Public posts only, and a relayed post arrives as the post it is rather than as a boost by the relay
- 💬 Quote controls: who may quote each of your posts (anybody, your followers, nobody), who already has, and a button that detaches one and tells their server
- 🔑 Authorized apps: every app holding a key to your account, with what it may do and when it was last used, and a button that signs one out — the page to open after losing a phone
- 🚪 Delete your Social account from Settings and keep your Nextcloud one: the posts, the follows, and a Delete to every server that knew you
- 🔕 Filtered notifications: the senders your notification policy is holding, one row each, with Show these and Dismiss — and a way to hide a whole server rather than its accounts one at a time
- 📜 Edit history: the "Edited" line under a post opens every version of it
- 🧳 Migration in both directions: the blocks, mutes and lists another network exported, read here; and your follows, followers, blocks, mutes and lists written back out one CSV at a time, the way Mastodon writes them
- 📅 Your year, as a report — Mastodon's #Wrapstodon: twelve months of what you posted and who arrived, the hashtags you used, the three posts that travelled furthest
- 🛡️ For moderators: what may trend (a hashtag, a link or a post kept out of Explore), the instance's custom emoji and its rules, all from the administration page rather than from occ

You can pin your own posts to the top of your profile, bookmark any post, and see which hashtags the instance is using most. This is a partial implementation of ActivityPub and of the Mastodon client API. Blocking, muting and reporting (with a moderation panel in the administration settings) are supported, as are locked accounts with approvable follow requests. Polls are fully supported: create your own, and view and vote on federated ones. Profiles carry an avatar, a banner image and up to four profile metadata fields, edited in the profile editor; a field naming a web page is marked as verified once that page links back with rel="me". Posts that link somewhere get a link preview card. Image (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, and HEIC from an iPhone where the server can read it), video (MP4, WebM, QuickTime) and audio attachments are supported, up to ten per post, each with alt text and a focal point. Quote posts carry the original author's permission on the wire, and the author decides who may quote each post and can take one back afterwards. Third-party Mastodon clients cannot reach the API yet, because it is served under the app's own path rather than at the domain root; there is no streaming API and no push subscriptions. A post can be translated where this Nextcloud has a translation provider.

sociallogin.description:
# Social Login

Make it possible to create users and log in via Telegram, OAuth, or OpenID.

For OAuth, you must create an app with certain providers. Login buttons will appear on the login page if an app ID is specified. Settings are located in the "Social login" section of the settings page.

## Installation

Log in to your Nextcloud installation as an administrator. Under "Apps", click "Download and enable" next to the "Social Login" app.

See below for setup and configuration instructions.

## Custom OAuth2/OIDC Groups

You can use groups from your custom provider. For this, specify the "Groups claim" in the custom OAuth2/OIDC provider settings. This claim should be returned from the provider in the `id_token` or at the user info endpoint. Multiple claims (comma separated) also supported - groups will be merged.
The format should be an `array` or a comma-separated string. E.g., (with a claim named `roles`):

```json
{"roles": ["admin", "user"]}
```
or
```json
{"roles": "admin,user"}
```

Nested claims are also supported. For example, `resource_access.client-id.roles` for:

```json
"resource_access": {
   "client-id": {
     "roles": [
       "client-role-1",
       "client-role-2"
     ]
   }
}
```

**DisplayName** support is also available:
```json
{"roles": [{"gid": 1, "displayName": "admin"}, {"gid": 2, "displayName": "user"}]}
```

You can use provider groups in two ways:

1. Map provider groups to existing Nextcloud groups.
2. Create provider groups in Nextcloud and associate them with users (if the appropriate option is enabled).

To sync groups on every login, ensure the "Update user profile every login" setting is checked.

## Examples for Groups

* Configure WSO2IS to return a roles claim with OIDC [here](https://medium.com/@dewni.matheesha/claim-mapping-and-retrieving-end-user-information-in-wso2is-cffd5f3937ff).
* [GitLab OIDC configuration to allow specific GitLab groups](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/blob/master/docs/sso/gitlab.md).

## Built-in OAuth Providers

Copy the link from a specific login button to get the correct "redirect URL" for OAuth app settings.

* [Amazon](https://developer.amazon.com/loginwithamazon/console/site/lwa/overview.html)
* [Apple](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/blob/master/docs/sso/apple.md)
* [Codeberg](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/blob/master/docs/sso/codeberg.md)
* [Discord](#configure-discord)
* [Facebook](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/blob/master/docs/sso/facebook.md)
* [GitHub](https://github.com/settings/developers)
* [GitLab](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/blob/master/docs/sso/gitlab.md)
* [Google](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/blob/master/docs/sso/google.md)
* [Keycloak](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/blob/master/docs/sso/keycloak.md)
* [Mail.ru](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/blob/master/docs/sso/mailru.md)
* **PlexTv**: Use any title as the app ID.
* [Telegram](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/blob/master/docs/sso/telegram.md)
* [Twitter](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/blob/master/docs/sso/twitter.md)

For details about Google's "Allow login only from specified domain" setting, see [#44](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/issues/44). Use a comma-separated list for multiple domains.

## Configuration

Add `'social_login_auto_redirect' => true` to `config.php` to automatically redirect unauthorized users to social login if only one provider is configured. To temporarily disable this (e.g., for local admin login), add `noredir=1` to the login URL: `https://cloud.domain.com/login?noredir=1`.

Configure HTTP client options using:
```php
  'social_login_http_client' => [
    'timeout' => 45,
    'proxy' => 'socks4://127.0.0.1:9050', // See <https://curl.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_PROXY.html> for allowed formats
  ],
```
in `config.php`.

### Configure a Provider via CLI

Use the `occ` utility to configure providers via the command line. Replace variables and URLs with your deployment values:
```bash
php occ config:app:set sociallogin custom_providers --value='{"custom_oidc": [{"name": "gitlab_oidc", "title": "Gitlab", "authorizeUrl": "https://gitlab.my-domain.org/oauth/authorize", "tokenUrl": "https://gitlab.my-domain.org/oauth/token", "userInfoUrl": "https://gitlab.my-domain.org/oauth/userinfo", "logoutUrl": "", "clientId": "$my_application_id", "clientSecret": "$my_super_secret_secret", "scope": "openid", "groupsClaim": "groups", "style": "gitlab", "defaultGroup": ""}]}'
```
For Docker, prepend `docker exec -t -uwww-data CONTAINER_NAME` to the command or run interactively via `docker exec -it -uwww-data CONTAINER_NAME sh`.

To inspect configurations:
```sql
mysql -u nextcloud -p nextcloud
Password: <yourpassword>

> SELECT * FROM oc_appconfig WHERE appid='sociallogin';
```
Or run:
```bash
docker exec -t -uwww-data CONTAINER_NAME php occ config:app:get sociallogin custom_providers
```

### Configure Discord

1. Create a Discord application at [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications).
2. Navigate to `Settings > OAuth2 > General`. Add a redirect URL: `https://nextcloud.mydomain.com/apps/sociallogin/oauth/discord`.
3. Copy the `CLIENT ID` and generate a `CLIENT SECRET`.
4. In Nextcloud, go to `Settings > Social Login`. Paste the `CLIENT ID` into "App id" and `CLIENT SECRET` into "Secret".
5. Select a default group for new users.
6. For group mapping, see [#395](https://github.com/zorn-v/nextcloud-social-login/pull/395).

## Hint

### Callback (Reply) URL
Copy the link from a login button on the Nextcloud login page and use it as the callback URL on your provider's site. To make the button visible temporarily, fill provider settings with placeholder data and update later.

If you encounter callback URL errors despite correct settings, ensure your Nextcloud server generates HTTPS URLs by adding `'overwriteprotocol' => 'https'` to `config.php`.

twofactor_email.description:
### A Two-Factor-Auth Provider using email

Nextcloud supports web logins with a second factor (two-factor authentication,
2FA). To support a certain type of 2FA, a "2FA provider" server app must be
installed. 2FA kicks in after the primary authentication stage (typically
username and password) were successful. This provider challenges the user to
enter a randomly generated authentication code (aka one-time password, OTP,
default: six digits). It sends that code to the user's primary email address
and expects the user to enter it on an additional second step web login page.

### Installation, activation and usage

As with any 2FA provider, two-factor email must be installed and enabled by a
Nextcloud server admin. Additionally, the Nextcloud must have a working email
server configured.

The user may set up any of the installed providers or even multiple. This
provider uses email to send the code and thus can only be enabled if an email
address is set in "Personal info". Mind that a user may not be able to log in
if that email address is invalid (or email server setup of the Nextcloud is
not working properly).

Admins with console access may enable and disable this provider for specified
users via "occ" command. Admins may also enforce 2FA for all users (or specific
groups) via "Admin Settings". This is a Nextcloud feature and not specific to
this provider. If enforced, users with no 2FA are prompted to enable any
installed provider (if they support that feature). This provider supports it
since v3. If the admin installs this provider and enforces 2FA, it should be
ensured that each user does have a valid email address.

Mind that, once a user enabled any 2FA provider, they can no longer use their
password in applications that don't support the web-based 2FA login flow. For
such applications, the user needs to create and use app passwords (to be found
at the bottom of "Personal Settings/Security").

twofactor_oath.description:
Configurable OATH two-factor authentication for Nextcloud, covering all three OATH algorithms in one provider.

- **TOTP** (RFC 6238), **HOTP** (RFC 4226) and **OCRA** challenge-response (RFC 6287), selectable per token
- Per-token hash algorithm (SHA-1 to SHA-512), digits (4 to 10), TOTP period or HOTP counter, and OCRA suite
- Custom or random secrets, with clear strength presets (128 to 640 bit) and secrets encrypted at rest
- A **Strict RFC** switch for safe, interoperable defaults, without losing the freedom to deviate
- Admin-managed enrollment for whole groups, with **bulk provisioning** (sorting, filtering, live validation), CSV export and paste import
- One-click **import from the bundled twofactor_totp**, so existing users switch over without being locked out
- Issuer icon embedded in the QR code, HOTP resynchronisation, and a software OCRA token for testing

Built for hardware OATH tokens and elevated requirements, alongside the simple, bundled twofactor_totp app. OATH (one-time passwords) is not the same as FIDO2/WebAuthn. See documentation for when to use which.

user_saml.description:
Using the SSO & SAML app of your Nextcloud you can make it easily possible to integrate your existing Single-Sign-On solution with Nextcloud. In addition, you can use the Nextcloud LDAP user provider to keep the convenience for users. (e.g. when sharing)
The following providers are supported and tested at the moment:

* **SAML 2.0**
	* OneLogin
	* Shibboleth
	* Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS)
	* Authentik

* **Authentication via Environment Variable**
	* Kerberos (mod_auth_kerb)

vereinsbuchhaltung.description:
**Accounting for nonprofit clubs – fully within your own Nextcloud.**

For treasurers of small and medium-sized clubs who don't run separate
accounting software and don't want their financial data in some provider's
cloud. Your data stays wherever your Nextcloud is hosted.

You don't need to be an accountant: in **simple mode** you record an "income"
or "expense" with amount, date and category – the app handles double-entry
bookkeeping in the background. If you'd rather set debit and credit yourself,
switch to expert mode.

**[▶ The app in two minutes (video, German)](https://youtu.be/eaF-tAQ_OOM)** –
import bank statements, assign transactions, evaluate and produce the annual
treasurer's report.

## The workflow

1. **Import a bank statement** – CSV-CAMT, CAMT.053 (XML) or MT940 from your
   online banking; the app detects the format from the content, the file
   extension doesn't matter. Transactions already present are recognized and
   skipped, even across formats. A watch folder can even pick up new
   statements on its own, without a manual import.
2. **Assign transactions** – every bank entry gets a counter-account. Rules
   handle recurring assignments (rent, membership fees, charges)
   automatically.
3. **Attach receipts** – photo or PDF, either in a Nextcloud folder of your
   choice or stored inside the app. Or as a watch folder: whatever you drop
   into it in the Files app can be picked when booking, and the overview
   reports what is not yet assigned to an entry.
4. **Evaluate and report** – treasurer's report for the general assembly,
   short report for board meetings, exports for the audit.

## What the app can do

- **Double-entry bookkeeping** with a freely definable chart of accounts; a
  standard chart of accounts for clubs is included
- **Treasurer's report** and **short report** as print-ready pages (Ctrl+P),
  optionally with your club's logo and accent color
- **Financial plan** with plan/actual comparison and freezable plan snapshots
- **Nonprofit status:** spheres following the German four-sphere model
  (ideational, asset management, purpose-related business, commercial
  business) and reserves per § 62 AO
- **Membership fees & SEPA direct debit** (optional, can be enabled as
  needed): member management with CSV import, direct debit mandates, fees
  with individual payment frequency, SEPA batch collection as a pain.008
  file for your bank – its own tab in the main navigation; if you don't need
  the module, you never see it
- **Open items** – keep track of unpaid receivables with due dates
- **Multi-year trend** and result per reporting group
- **Freely definable fiscal year:** it does not have to match the calendar
  year – October–September, the school year August–July or half-year
  periods (semesters) are just as possible
- **Year-end closing:** a finalized fiscal year can no longer be changed;
  continuous, gap-free posting numbers per fiscal year
- **Change log:** who changed what, and when
- **Roles:** administrator, bookkeeper and auditor – the audit role gets
  read access to everything without being able to change anything
- **On the go:** dedicated view for smartphones, photograph receipts
  directly
- **Annual audit:** all receipts for a year as a ZIP, print-ready quick
  guide for the auditor, completeness check of posting numbers

A **sample club** can be created with one click to try everything out
risk-free, and removed again with another click.

Existing data from "zero Buchhaltung" can be taken over via its xbuc files.

Full manual in German and English: see documentation.

workspace.description:
# Description

Workspace allows managers to :
- Create shared workspaces
- Delegate management of each workspace to users (workspace managers) in order for them to:
    - choose members
    - create groups
    - configure advanced permissions on workspace folders
- All through a simple unified interface, designed to simplify your users' experience and make them autonomous

It is necessary to install the Team folders app for the Workspace app to work.

# App configuration

Before using Workspace, you must configure the app, following these important steps:

- Limit the Workspace app to specific groups : in your "application management" administrator interface, limit the application to the following groups: "GeneralManager" and "WorkspacesManagers".

- Configure Team folders for Workspace:
    - In "Settings" > "Team folders" > "Group folder admin delegation" section, add the group "GeneralManager" to the **first** field, and the group "WorkspacesManagers" to the **second** field

If you are using a major version of Nextcloud lower than Nextcloud 25, please follow the instructions provided on [GitHub](https://github.com/arawa/workspace). 

For more information, please visit [our website](https://www.arawa.fr/solutions/produits-arawa/arawa-workspace-for-nextcloud/) (french content).

For more details, please go to the [admin documentation](https://github.com/arawa/workspace/blob/main/README.md#installation), or [user documentation](https://github.com/arawa/workspace/tree/main/docs/user-guide/from-3.X.X).

x2mail.description:
X2Mail is webmail for Nextcloud with native SSO.

Log in to Nextcloud through your OIDC provider and open Email. X2Mail passes your OIDC token to the mail server via OAuth2 (OAUTHBEARER/XOAUTH2), so users never enter a separate mail password or see a second login form.

X2Mail uses Nextcloud's own APIs. It needs no external services and no database of its own.

### Nextcloud integration
- Contacts: read, create and edit contacts in all your Nextcloud address books
- Files: attach files from Nextcloud Files, save emails and attachments there
- Calendar: add ICS invitations to your calendar, with a warning if the event already exists
- Dashboard: widget for unread mail, with automatic OIDC token refresh
- Search: find emails through Nextcloud Unified Search
- SSO: IMAP access with your OIDC login instead of stored credentials

### Features
- SSO without extra configuration in X2Mail: OAUTHBEARER and XOAUTH2 are detected automatically and the token is refreshed before it expires
- Nextcloud admins manage X2Mail in the Nextcloud settings, without a separate admin password
- Setup wizard with preflight checks for IMAP, SMTP and OIDC, plus token diagnostics
- Nextcloud theme with light and dark mode
- Server-side mail filters (Sieve)
- Multiple sender identities
- OpenPGP and S/MIME
- Command line: `occ x2mail:setup`, `occ x2mail:status`

### Setup
```
occ x2mail:setup --imap-host mail.example.com --domain example.com --sieve
```

### Requirements
- Nextcloud 33 to 35, PHP 8.3+
- Mail server with OAuth2 SASL (OAUTHBEARER) on IMAP and SMTP submission; tested with Dovecot 2.4+ with Postfix, and with Stalwart 0.16+
- `user_oidc` with an OIDC provider; tested with Keycloak

xfiles.description:
X-Files is a photo vault that protects your most sensitive images with an
independent password, completely isolated from Files, Photos, Memories,
WebDAV, and Search.

**Features:**
- Password-protected vault (independent from Nextcloud login)
- Real file isolation via AppData (invisible to other apps)
- Auto-lock after configurable timeout
- Brute-force protection on unlock attempts
- Thumbnail gallery when unlocked
- Recovery key for password reset
- Download recovery key as formatted text file
- Change password and settings from within the vault
- Auto-lock when browser tab is closed

**Security:**
- Images stored in AppData (not in user filesystem)
- Other apps (Files, Photos, Memories) cannot see vault content
- WebDAV and desktop/mobile clients cannot access vault images
- Vault password hashed with Argon2id
- Session-based unlock with configurable timeout
- Brute-force and rate-limit protection

Lock your secrets. Trust no one.

yoomail.description:
**🚀 YooMail — A high-performance mail app for Nextcloud**

YooMail is a secondary development (fork) of Nextcloud Mail, focused on **realtime delivery** and **instant reading** of emails.

- **⚡ Realtime email delivery** — A built-in Workerman + IMAP IDLE daemon pushes new emails within seconds; no manual refresh or polling required.
- **🚀 Instant body caching** — Message bodies are persistently cached after first render, so reopening a message is nearly instant.
- **📥 Multiple mail accounts** — Personal and company account? No problem, and a nice unified inbox. Connect any IMAP account.
- **🔒 Send & receive encrypted mails** — Using the great [Mailvelope](https://mailvelope.com) browser extension.
- **📬 Deep Nextcloud integration** — Contacts, Calendar and Files.

## Base version

This app is built on top of Nextcloud Mail **5.10.12**, with compatibility fixes for special-use folders (Sent / Deleted / Drafts) on some Chinese mail providers (Tencent ExMail / QQ Mail, NetEase Mail, etc.).
